content: We really enjoyed our stay at Cheetah Rocks. We went on two different days because the combined tour was already fully booked. But we don't regret it at all and would do it again in a heartbeat! On the Great Wildlife Tour, we were in a larger group and received precise instructions about what we could and couldn't do. I appreciate that the animals can always retreat if things get too overwhelming for them. We experienced so many animals up close: bush babies, monkeys, lemurs, and even the white lions and the tiger made an appearance. A dream came true for me when it was Latifa's turn and we were allowed to take photos with her. And I'd also like to mention that she could have left at any time if she had wanted to, so I don't think it's animal cruelty or profiteering. After all, their livelihood has to be financed somehow. Meat is expensive, and the vet costs money too. Jenny then introduced us to Beppo. She's simply a wonderful, genuine, and animal-loving person. On our second visit, we did the VIP Otter Experience. What was the advantage? No groups, just my husband, me, and the otters! JJ explained everything to us, and we learned a lot about otters—that they're cute but can also be quite different. Then it started, and we got to splash around with the otters and feed them. I was especially taken with Captain Jack, the sweet little one; I hope everything went well with the introduction to his new companion. And when we said goodbye to the otters, JJ said he'd like to introduce us to someone else he hadn't been able to show us the day before… and voilà, we got to visit a cheetah again and brush and pet it! I don't know how it's spelled (Sharqui?). We also received so much information about the different animals, and of course, there were many sad stories too! But now they're in loving hands and will be well cared for. Thank you all for your wonderful work. ❤️

content:
I must admit, the first time I saw this place online when researching our family trip to Zanizbar I was skeptical, but goodness me, how pleased I was to be proved so wrong. These animals are so incredibly cared for, all of the training they are given is not for entertainment but enrichment and ensures easier, less stressful administration of medical needs. The care that the owner and her wonderful team have, including Charlie & JJ for these animals is so evident.
For my Mum's birthday I purchased the otter experience. It was quite simply incredible. Our guide and keeper was Charlie, who was not only lovely, but so informative and he loved those otters so much, and it was evident that they adored him right back. He is the father of otters!!
As a full family we did the full tour today, something that we will never forget. Being able to stroke a cheetah, have lemurs and monkeys bounce onto your shoulders, bush babies crawl into your lap and even meet their newest resident Zebra for a neck scratch..... wow!!
It is so clear how cared for these animals are, they run on only positive reinforcements (mainly food) and each of the interactions are always on the animals terms (the primates have to choose to jump on you!) The rest are free to leave from the people if they wish and return to their enclosures.
You hear so many horror stories as an animal lover of drugged animals, declawed cats etc and Cheetahs Rock couldn't be further from this. It is truly a place where the animals are cherished and rescued from often awful situations, working with all the relevant authorities to ensure rare species conservation, rescue lions from apartment buildings when kept as pets etc.....
If you're on the fence, do it. As a proud animal lover with a massive interest in animal welfare, I can say it was one of the most amazing things I've ever done. Well done Jenny and team; and thank you for all that you do.

But they and the employees also have to live, so please don't write judgments here with your eyes closed, and that was putting it nicely.

Laura and Patrick

Despite what the detractors of this exceptional place might say, we absolutely loved our experience at this rescue center.
Of course, it's important to understand the center's educational and dedicated mission. Yes, the animals are in cages, but most of them are endangered, and the goal is to preserve them and try to breed them in the best possible conditions.
As for the other animals, they were rescued from deplorable conditions (mistreatment, destined for the pet trade or to be eaten in certain restaurants).
So, yes, hats off to the work done by these truly passionate people who share their love for animals and the essential respect they deserve. 😃👍🏻

I'm a bit late with this review, about seven or eight years, but out of respect for the team, here it is:

The cheekier of the cubs (Marek or something like that?) playfully nipped me in the ribs, and I was as proud as punch of the little scar afterward. Sadly, it's faded.
I definitely got the impression that the animals were well cared for, and for us human visitors, it was unforgettable.
Sure, it's quite an expensive activity for an afternoon, but it was definitely worth it – and the animals can't exactly pay for their own food.
So, thank you and best regards to Jenny and the team, and also to the son, who I'm sure has become a great tiger tamer!

Getting in touch with the animals, hearing the stories of their recovery, and seeing the loving care was a wonderful experience. You interacted with a zebra, bush babies (baby galagos), monkeys, lemurs, dik-diks (small antelopes), giant horned tortoises from Madagascar... and finally, the mascot... Latifa the cheetah. There are also five lions, two hyenas, and a Bengal tiger.
Book online with taxi service included...the experience is a bit pricey...but the goal is noble.
Good luck with your future endeavors.

content: In the first part of the Wildlife tour we were introduced to a Zebra named Chaka. At first I wasn't too sure how I felt when the handler started making Chaka perform some simple tricks, almost in a circus-like manner. But it soon became clear that he was trying to show an audience who for the most part was completely ignorant of Zebras that they are highly intelligent and emotionally sensitive animals. And it works. Because I noticed that at the beginning of the presentation only a handful of people in my group were willing to interact with Chaka and hand feed him some carrots. But after seeing him play fetch and with a ball everyone wanted to pet him at the end. Next we were given a chance to interact with a variety of monkeys, feeding them and petting them as well as peacocks, an endangered species of deer as well lemurs and tortoises. The sanctuary also has 5 white lions, all very impressive, especially the alpha male Arslan, a couple of striped hyenas and a couple of tigers. And finally everyone in our group had a picture taken by the handlers with one of the cheetas resident. The whole tour took about 4 hours and was highly educational and fun. We felt safe and comfortable at all times and I strongly suggest you visit Cheetah's Rock during your stay in Zanzibar.

content:
We visited Cheetah's Rock yesterday and we are overwhelmed.
It was the absolute highlight of our vacation.
It's wonderful to see that there are still people like those at Cheetah's Rock who aren't just in it for the money.
The animals are treated with such respect and love. In my opinion, it's precisely this respectful and loving approach that allows you to get closer to the animals than anywhere else. The team on site does an outstanding job and commands my utmost respect!
We are absolutely blown away! I love nature and animals, and I prefer to explore them "by chance" and leave them in peace. Just observe, enjoy the experience, and then move on. With the bushbabies, for example, it was lovely to see that when one of them retreated, it was truly left alone. Here, the animals can still decide for themselves whether and how intensely they want to interact.
Mario led this expedition with great professionalism and humor. It's clear that all the staff have a deep respect for the animals. It's wonderful to see that there are still places where animals are treated the way they deserve.
You gladly put up with the countless mosquito bites.
At some point, I didn't even want to take any more photos because I was so fascinated by everything and just wanted to observe.
The only "negative" point:
After this experience, we regret not booking the combined tour ;-).
All the best to Jenny, Mario, and all the staff at Cheetah's Rock for this extraordinary experience and the fantastic work they do here!
Best regards,
Markus & Christina Wollmann

content: On various forums you will find a lot of different discussions about this place. It is not my job to convince you of either side of the argument. For me, visiting this place was an amazing lifelong experience. It is worth being in a place where, in my opinion, animals are cared for with a big heart and their stories are told with passion. It doesn't matter if you go on safari to the mainland afterwards because it's a different experience. We were picked up by a car from Paje and driven to Cheetah's Rock. We took one person along the way. On the spot, we sign a statement that we will not blame the resort for any damage to health blown up by animals. Sounds serious but the crew cares about our safety very much and they have a lot of experience. During your stay at the resort, the staff makes sure that we take a picture with the animal ... we don't have to worry about it. During the four-hour stay, we will get to know the stories of our heroes, we will be able to touch most of them or feed and meet the amazing founder and her crew. The cost of the Great Wildlife Tour is USD 160. You can say it's a lot but remember that you are helping to keep these animals and besides, the safari costs several times more and you will never be as close to wild animals as in Cheetah's Rock.

content:
My husband and I booked a day-long excursion to this delightful animal sanctuary. In the morning, we enjoyed a private playtime with the otters. We got to provide enrichment time treats and stimulation while learning about their stories and the species as a whole. With some extra time remaining, we got to meet some of the big cats at the rescue privately. That was unforgettable!
In the afternoon, we got to meet several really cool animals. We fell in love with a white tigeress and chuffed with her mate. We got tiger kisses and scratched them behind the ears. The rescue is doing really great work here. Some amputees, some poacher rescues, some apartment pet rescues, some rehabs that will be released. Pretty impressive. Very clean. Very educational. The animal ambassadors are helping the rescue raise money. Yea, it was commercial, but for a good cause. The animals are not ever forced to perform on demand, and it is clear that their welfare takes top priority.
Thank you, Katerina and Danny and the whole staff at Cheetahs Rock for an unforgettable adventure.

content:
I wish I could give negative stars to this place.
DO NOT WASTE time and money ON Cheetah Rock, there is so much more Zanzibar has to offer, this highly commercialized operation is not worth it.
Plus the owner is mentally unstable person who threatens anyone who dares to not love her place or making money.
This place (the owner in particular) portray themselves as animal lovers and Cheetah Rock as wild life caring place but in reality it’s a money making scheme that milks tourists and offers zoo/circus like photo opportunities.
Zebra trained to fetch and pick up and kick ball, monkeys eating pasta, etc. has nothing to do with wild life or care for wild animals.
They take a group of 40-50 people thru 1/2 dozen animal enclosures (pretty small ones at that) and spend most time for every tourist to take pictures. This experience takes 4 hours not because you see or experience much, but rather because it’s lengthy photo-op session, you see very little in reality.
The owner of the place offered lengthy and semi-hysterical lecture on how terrible humans are towards animals and how COVID was fake (because pandemic and decline in tourism obviously impacted her income stream).
We left the tour after 1.5 hours as it was both boring and offensive for anyone who likes wild life rather than Zoo-circus like experiences.
We did mention to the person who was fetching our car that we found experience both disappointing and overpriced. And in response the owner yelled in front of the whole group of 40 at hour daughter (who stayed behind with her friends) that we blackmailed her staff. Ridiculous!!!!
She clearly throws a fit and writes threatening responses for any non-positive review (checkout Tripadvisor reviews), including mine.
When I reached out to the place and requested an apology for such outrageous behaviour after our disappointing experience, they couldn’t care less and didn't bother to even respond.
Save yourself time and money while in Zanzibar, DO NOT WASTE IT ON Cheetah Rock. Zanzibar has so much real beauty and animal life to offer.

content:
This was one of our highlights in Zanzibar.
Can you really get close to the animals and touch them? YES! (except the big cats)
First we saw the Zebra which you could feed and play little games with. Wow.
Then we went to different kinds of monkeys which we were feeding from our hands. Some you could touch, some hop on your shoulder and hands. You can even touch the peacock sometimes.
Our last station was the big cats like tigers, lions and pumas. Those were of course behind a fence but still we were able to get really close to them. What an experience!
Lastly we were able to make photos with a cheetah and touch his hindside. This was awe inspiring and an amazing experience.
The staff always gave the backstory to the animals, told us what to look for and consider when getting close to them. We felt very well taken care of and instructed. They talk passionately about the animals and those look well fed and taken care of.
One more highlight was the talk with the founder who talked about the project, how the animals came to her and struggles she faced while building up the program. Such passion! Admirable.
All in all we had a great time, took nice pictures and now have impressions of a life time. It was well worth the money and we are glad that we visited this place.

Poor humanity!
The underlying humanitarian effort is good, helping animals in distress is undeniable, and people here are doing their utmost to save these creatures.
However, that doesn't justify everything. Here, they allow themselves to put on real shows to impress tourists. A poor zebra worked in a zoo, and Cheeta's Rock rescues him to play ball in front of forty or so tourists seated on a platform: it's a circus.
The bush babies, a small breed of nocturnal monkeys, will be fed by you, in broad daylight.

Only thing that was a bit annoying - there are too many people on the tour at the same time (about 35-40 on ours) and it gets really crowded, you barely get opportunity to meet the animals by yourself, because some people just won't let you. I'd say 20 should be the max.
However! Where else you get the chance to see such rare animals as the white lion, golden tiger or angonoka/plougshare tortoise? There are just few left in the wild.
If you have the chance, visit this place and see for yourself.
Mind you, this is not your regular petting zoo. If the animal doesn't want to be touched, you have to respect it.

Was it worth it? Absolutely.

content:
It was an unforgettable experience.
On our previous safari, we were able to observe lions, zebras, dik-diks, and other animals in their natural habitat. However, it's also wonderful to know that there are places for animals who haven't had such a lucky start in life.
One might wonder whether Cheetah's Rock and its interaction with visitors is truly the right way to treat the animals, especially after watching certain Netflix documentaries about so-called "animal rescue centers." It's easy to become skeptical.
After visiting and speaking directly with Jenny and the Cheetah's Rock team, we can confidently say that the animals are doing exceptionally well. They live in large, beautifully designed, species-appropriate enclosures, and all interaction with visitors is entirely voluntary. The team's deep connection and love for the animals is evident, and it's clear that everything is being done to ensure their well-being.
With this peace of mind, experiencing the residents of Cheetah's Rock up close is all the more rewarding. During the very direct interaction, the backstory of each animal is shared, along with other facts, so you can learn quite a bit.
In our opinion, the entrance fee shouldn't just be seen as an opportunity to take unique photos, but above all as a donation to help give the animals a dignified life. We think the concept of Cheetah's Rock is fantastic, and we will never forget this special day.

content:
We had a very exceptional experience at Cheetah's Rock. First, I can confirm all the good reviews for this place: The team cares a lot about every single animal and they are doing whatever is possible to ensure a good life for them. Sure, it is stunning to get in close contact with these animals, but what is even more important is to see that there is a lovely place for animals which can not be released to the wild anymore. With your entry fee, you will definitely save lives!
But now I want to explain why our visit was something special.
The plan to visit Africa and to go on a safari was our dream for a long time. My girlfriend's favorite animal is the zebra, and she was so lucky when we finally booked the trip to Tanzania. content:
This is a nice place to see different exotic animals up close but if you are expecting a lot of interaction than you are at the wrong place!
Here they like to talk about the animal, it's sad story and the species struggles in the wilderness. So if you are an animal fanatic and really interested in facts than this is the place.
Furthermore this place is extremely commercial which is a big disappointment: the price is very high just to see animals an hear their long stories. Their tours are also made of about 40 people so when you finally get the chance to touch an animal you only have about one second.
I've visited a number of other animal rescues in Africa that were way better: less commercial, a lot more natural and with a lot more interaction.
I've gone home with mixed feelings after my visit and hope this review will help someone!

Animals - folks, let me tell you, you get up close and personal with the animals. From monkeys, lemurs to Cheetah’s and tigers. The experience was surreal. You really get to learn about the history of the animal and how they were rescued and re-homed in a nourishing environment.
The staff - The staff are incredibly professional, welcoming and definitely kept us entertained. They made sure that our safety was a priority and kept us briefed throughout. Very impressed with the service.
Price - at first, it might seem like the tour is expensive but it was all worth the money. Once you see the effort and funding that goes into creating this experience, it’s a small price to pay.
In conclusion, if you’re visiting Zanzibar and if you’re an animal lover, this is a must do activity. Highly recommended. 🙂

content: Fantastic informative and enthusiastic guided tour which tells you all about the animals and how they ended up at cheetahs rock. Some very sad stories of horrific animal abuse but all the animals are healthy and well looked after now :) not like a zoo at all. You get some great close encounters and fantastic pictures. Cheetahs rock takes in all sort of animals in need and have very big enclosures with natural grass and plants all around. The puma we see on the tour has been trained to enter her transport box voluntarily with no stress for medical access if she ever needs it so she's not kept in a cage all day as some reviews say. I feel very good and confident that my money is going to an excellent sanctuary and animal welfare is not a concern here at all!

content:
This was an excellent experience that I would highly recommend if you have some free time in Zanzibar. First, I want to say that this is a TRUE animal sanctuary through and through (based on the research I did before visiting and also everything I observed while there.) I have visited other rescues in other parts of the world that because of political or economic pressure, have made certain compromises to stay open and be able to maintain operations, but at some expense to their animals. In the situations they are in, they reason that the animals are at least better off there than where they were before (and usually they are), but they have to make their location more lucrative in order to stay afloat. At Cheetah’s Rock, I didn’t witness any such compromise. Their policies always appeared to put animal welfare and visitor safety over gimmick-y tourist attractions (which is much rarer than you would think!), while still maintaining an enjoyable and educational experience for visitors. For example, once lions reach maturity (they are much more aggressive than cheetahs when fully grown), they no longer allow photos with visitors- which is the safest and most humane thing! —
For a more detailed account:
A round trip driver to and from your hotel (for most areas on the island) is included in the price. Our driver was on time, courteous, and got me excited for the visit. Upon arrival, our guide, Shane, was very welcoming and told us what we could expect, briefed us on safety procedures, and was very up front about any risks with specific animals and experiences. It was raining when we arrived, so we started under a covered area, where we met an adorable zebra, Chaka. We were told how staff only use positive reinforcement to build trust in the animals, which not only allow visitors to interact, but more importantly, allow vets to treat the animals without using tranquilizing drugs for routine check-ups, which is much healthier. Then we met a gorgeous puma (who was in heat!) and were told her heartbreaking story before being rescued. We then got to go into an enclosure with some lemurs, who we could feed as they sat on our shoulders, and one of the rarest species in the world, Ploughshare Tortoises!! We also visited a psyches blue monkey and two playful vervets. One of my favorite encounters was with the bush babies! The are super interested in you- sniffing you, preening your hair and giving you lots of love. Then, we were served champagne and refreshments before meeting Aslan the lion! He stays in his enclosure for safety, BUT, volunteers who would rise to the challenges can start by making eye contact, leading to a race up and down the grounds. I volunteered and it was so cool to connect with this lion and get him excited to race, switching back and changing direction while maintaining eye contact. We later saw some beautiful and very rare golden tabby tigers. Finally, of course, we were able to pose with the cheetahs. There were two separate cheetah encounters, both allowing photo opportunities.
The only advice I would give is that someone in your group take your pictures (allowed only for the first cheetah encounter). I was a solo traveler so relied on the staff to take pictures and unfortunately did not get a single usable picture with the cheetahs (almost all were blurry or the cheetah was cut out of the frame). But, the couple that was in my car took their own photos and were very satisfied with theirs (and were a little more pushy with getting photo time). If I went again, I would just have another guest take my pictures☺️. On the second cheetah encounter, our group was a bit time pressured and because of the rain, the sunlight was gone, but we were still able to get very close to an even bigger cheetah and learn about why some were named after the royal family in Dubai. We later saw the adorable otters when passing outside their “night house”.
Thank you Cheetah’s Rock for maintaining your integrity and staying true to your mission❤️❤️

content:
We started our experience at Cheetah's Rock on the first day with the VIP Otter Experience. It was such a wonderful and amazing experience to feed the little Otter pirates and play in the water with these lively and joyful animals, which were full of energy. They made us smile the full time, we immediately fell in love with Bloody Mary, Cpt. Hook, Cpt. Blackbeard and Cpt. Jack Sparrow. There won’t be any other way than to fully enjoy this encounter. We are recommending the program to everyone. A big thank you as well for Leaveil and Stephan who made us feel very comfortable. They did a fantastic job, they were very kind, friendly, also took pictures about us and the animals and could always answer our questions. They ensured that the animals were always looked after while we (and they) played with them. This created a very pleasant atmosphere.
The Great Wildlife Experience took place on the next day. The tour starts with a welcome coconut water and a mandatory briefing. From the beginning you could see with what dedication, love and passion the employees in Cheetah‘s Rock look after the animals. Their well-being always comes first and is their top priority. They are making no profits out of the tours, all the money goes directly to the animals and helps the team sustain their operations. They are not getting any support from the government, that’s why the entrance fee for such an experience is more than justified. We learned a lot about their vision and goals and about the current situation concerning the flora and fauna in Zanzibar. That’s why their conservation work is even more important. From the staff we learned a lot about the animals at Cheetah‘s Rock. About their species but especially about their individual, mostly very sad back story. The most of the animals are rescued and adopted and due to ongoing physical impairments they will never be released to the wild as it would mean their certain death. At Cheetah‘s Rock they can live a happy, sheltered life in a large and spacious enclosure, which is adapted to their natural habitat. With so many different wild animals living in one place it is of course necessary to have fence between the different enclosures as a safety restraint. The resident Zoologist Stephan had a great deal of knowledge and could answer all the visitor questions in detail. The same applies for Leaveil and the rest of the employees, who led the group through the afternoon in a well-structured manner.
One of the highlights of course was the interaction with the different animals. This was again an experience for a lifetime. For example the soccer play with the zebra stallion Chaka, or having the opportunity to sit beside the cheetah Maktoum and touch him. Or feeding the bush babies, lemurs or monkeys treats while they are jumping from shoulder to shoulder, or helping the white lion Aslan having his 10kg meat per day, while having a refreshment for yourself with sparkling wine or water. It is very nice to see what a great deal of trust there is between the trainers and the animals, which is transferred to the visitors. For example the zebra stallion Chaka is trained to loose its fear of people and to build trust in order to get medical care. That is very important because at Cheetah‘s Rock the animals are not declawed, defanged, drugged in order to treat them nor forced to do anything by force. The interaction with the trainer or the visitors also enriches their lives so that they do not get bored.
We definitely recommend visiting Cheetah‘s Rock and if it’s possible to book both available programs. You do not only get educated very well, you also get the opportunity to get very close to a lot of wild animals, to touch and feed them, which leaves you with a breathtaking feeling. At Cheetah‘s Rock they mediate perfect consciousness for wildlife conservation. Your visit will not only enrich your, but also the animals life. A big thank you to the staff for making it an unforgettable experience and providing us two of the best days of our lives.
Kinga & Benedikt

content:
Sure, $160 is a lot of money; but for us, it was more than worth it. They house rescued animals and do a lot of educational work. Very informative and important, but you have to be open to it and also take a good look at your own behavior.
Besides zebras, bush babies, lemurs, and tortoises, they also have hyenas, white lions, tigers, and cheetahs for you to experience up close. If you want, you can go into some of the enclosures and pet the animals. They aren't sedated with medication or anything like that; instead, the trainers have built up a great deal of trust in people, so they can then pose for photos, etc. I didn't dare to do it myself, but my husband went into the enclosure and had some amazing moments with the big cats.
Between the different animals, there's always the opportunity to use the restroom with a guide. Champagne or water is also offered for refreshment.
The animals' sometimes very sad stories are presented vividly and humorously.
In our opinion, a must for every visitor to Zanzibar!

If you want, you can go into some of the enclosures and pet the animals.
They aren't sedated with medication or anything like that; instead, the trainers have built up a great deal of trust in people, so they can then pose for photos, etc.
I didn't dare to do it myself, but my husband went into the enclosure and had some amazing moments with the big cats.
Between the different animals, there's always the opportunity to use the restroom with a guide.
Champagne or water is also offered for refreshment.
The animals' sometimes very sad stories are presented vividly and humorously.
In our opinion, a must for every visitor to Zanzibar!

content:
It all goes down to your expectations and why you’re here.
If you’re here because of your love for animals, then you came to the right place. If you’re here because of the good cause of protecting endangered animals, then you’re definitely in the right place. But if you’re here to have sufficient time interacting one-on-one with the big cats, then you’ll likely be disappointed.
Here’s the itinerary:
1)) you arrive and get welcomed with fresh coconut water.
2)) you wait for everybody else to arrive, approximately 30 in total
3)) you get briefed for an hour about safety procedures, their mission, global climate etc. by an enthusiast that you’d enjoy listening to.
4)) you start with a Zebra interaction (feeding, playing with and petting) that takes about an hour, feels childish but yet entertaining.
5)) you move to Bush Monkeys interaction then to Lemur (so-called Lima Monkey), then to Dik-Dik, then to a rare specie of tortoises and peacocks. You get to see also a gorgeous rescued Cougar in a cage. That’s another 2 hours of feeding and petting.
6)) here comes the long waited gorgeous majestic 5 years old white lion. Of course you get to learn about it and see it from behind the cage. You get to feed it from behind the cage too.
7)) then you’re walked and briefed from behind the cage while they feed two cubs a Liger and a Tiger. Both are breathtakingly beautiful.
8)) this is followed by a photo shoot with two beautiful Cheetahs inside their enclosure but without any interaction more than petting its back while being photographed for few seconds, for the next in turn to do the same.
9)) lastly you’re surprised by meeting two young cubs (lion and tiger) who got walked on a leash separately to get close to the audience to pet their back as they swiftly walk past them.
Personally I feel like every one-on-one interaction is rushed due to the large number of the audience from start to finish. And especially when it comes to the big cats, I feel I left Cheetah’s Rock longing for more than what I got. I was told there’s a VIP experience that provides that, but personally I didn’t know about it, and even if I did I’d not have known what to expect from the original one verses the VIP one. Therefore I hope my review helps future visitors to decide.

content: At my request, we also visited Cheetah's Rock during our honeymoon in Zanzibar. However, instead of a joyful excursion, we quickly lost all enjoyment of the tour due to all the sad stories of abuse, murder, and who knows what else. :-( The group was so huge (almost 40 people) that, as an animal lover, I found it unacceptable. The zebra was treated like it was in a circus and had to perform tricks. I don't feel the animals were mistreated at all, but well, I still didn't feel good about it. We visitors were given the impression that we shouldn't be there, that they only run the tours to make money: period. Animal welfare comes before human well-being. This was emphasized more than once. I had wanted to fulfill my dream of touching a cheetah. Unfortunately, I was unlucky and was (luckily only lightly!) nipped on the knee by one of the two leopards roaming around. I panicked so much, I didn't know if I could say anything without provoking the animal. Luckily, it left me alone. That was enough for one day. The day was very tiring; the highlight was the lemurs and bush babies. At least you were allowed to pet them, even if it was very chaotic due to the large number of visitors. I would I wouldn't recommend anyone go there. It's better to donate the money; that will help the animals more.

Animals belong to the nature and not in circus or shows or outside shops to drag more customers in the shops.

content: It's a petting zoo. You go into cages, sit down, and then they let tame animals into your cage. You can feed them (they give you something to eat), touch them, and take photos. And so on, from cage to cage. Security is very high, there are staff nearby, everything is thought out, and there are a variety of animals: a puma, a cheetah, a zebra, a tiger, a galago, an indri, and turtles. We fed a lion in a cage and gave him meat. The lion was adorable, petted and well-fed, and the video shows he's very friendly with people. At the end of the tour, they give you champagne. What I didn't like: there were a lot of people, and the presenter talks a lot, A LOT, A LOT! It just got tiresome. It's worth a one-time visit! A photo hugging a tame cheetah outdoors, an indri on your shoulder, galagos everywhere—well, it's Africa!

It's really worth going there.
We were skeptical at first, too.

2. Because it seemed quite expensive, but that's how they finance themselves, and they don't receive any support from the government.
You can experience the animals up close, and they're really well cared for.
They're committed to their conservation, and they provide lots of information about the animals, their behavior, and how you can contribute to their protection.
Everything is also very well organized. The animals aren't harassed, and their habitat is respected.
I think it's worthwhile to support such a project and the dedication behind it. 😊

content:
Our visit to Forodhani Gardens was one of the most lively and enjoyable experiences in Zanzibar. Located right along the seafront in Stone Town, this place completely transforms as the evening sets in.
During the day, it’s a calm space by the ocean where you can take a relaxed walk and enjoy the sea breeze. But the real charm comes alive in the evening when the gardens turn into a bustling food market. The entire area fills up with local food stalls, the aroma of freshly cooked seafood and snacks, and a vibrant crowd of both locals and tourists.
We loved the energy of the place. There’s something happening everywhere — people gathering around food counters, trying out different dishes, and just enjoying the atmosphere. It’s a great spot to experience local street food and flavors in a very authentic setting.
What also makes it special is the setting. Being right by the water, you can enjoy your food while looking out at the ocean, especially during sunset when the sky changes colors — it’s a beautiful sight.
Overall, Forodhani Gardens is not just about food — it’s about the experience. The combination of great local flavors, a lively atmosphere, and a scenic seaside location makes it a must-visit when you’re in Stone Town.

content:
Forodhani Gardens is one of the most vibrant and memorable places to visit in Stone Town, Zanzibar. Located along the seafront, this public garden transforms every evening into a lively night food market that attracts both locals and tourists. As the sun sets over the Indian Ocean, the area fills with the aroma of grilled seafood, spices, and freshly prepared street food.
One of the most popular dishes is the famous Zanzibar pizza, a unique stuffed flatbread that can be made sweet or savory. Visitors can also enjoy mishkaki grilled meat skewers, samosas, urojo soup, and a variety of freshly squeezed fruit juices. The food is affordable, and there are many options to choose from, making it a great place to sample local flavors.
The atmosphere at Forodhani is energetic and social. Vendors call out to customers, friends gather to eat together, and children play nearby. The ocean breeze and beautiful sunset views add to the experience. Although it can become crowded and busy at night, the lively environment is part of its charm.
Overall, Forodhani Gardens offers an authentic taste of Zanzibar’s culture, cuisine, and community life.

content:
The Forodhani Gardens (also known as the Jubilee Gardens and, more recently, as Forodhani Park) [1] are a small park in the historic city of Stone Town, Zanzibar, Tanzania. They are located along Stone Town's main waterfront, directly opposite its most famous buildings: the House of Wonders and the Old Fort.
The gardens are especially busy after sunset, when tourists and locals gather at a popular street food market in the main square to dine and enjoy the delights of Swahili and Zanzibari cuisine, such as grilled seafood, samoosas, cassava, and sweet potatoes.
On July 31, 2009, the Aga Khan held a groundbreaking ceremony to inaugurate a revitalized park.
The rehabilitation was undertaken by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture (AKTC) at a cost of $3 million (3.9 billion shillings), compared to initial estimates of $2.4 million (over 3 billion shillings).
The renovation included the restoration of pedestrian walkways, landscaping, infrastructure modernization, the addition of lighting, a new sewage system and utilities, and the rehabilitation of the waterfront promenade in front of the park.

Nestled in the heart of Stone Town, The Forodhani Hotel offers an authentic and charming experience for travelers seeking cultural immersion in Zanzibar. Its prime location, directly across from the famous Forodhani Gardens and a short stroll from the seafront, makes it ideal for exploring the island’s vibrant history, food, and local life.
The rooms are simple yet comfortable, equipped with air conditioning, clean bathrooms, and traditional Swahili décor that reflects the heritage of the island. Some rooms offer sea views, enhancing the coastal atmosphere of your stay. The rooftop terrace is a hidden gem – perfect for catching sunsets or enjoying breakfast with a view.
The staff are friendly, helpful, and welcoming, always ready to assist with directions, tours, or special requests. While it’s not a luxury hotel, Forodhani provides excellent value for money and is ideal for travelers who prioritize location, cultural charm, and warm hospitality.
Overall, The Forodhani Hotel is a great choice for those who want to feel the pulse of Stone Town, enjoy local flavors, and stay within walking distance of major attractions like the Old Fort, House of Wonders, and bustling night markets.
Highly recommended for budget-conscious explorers!

The Heart of Zanzibar’s Street Food Scene
Forodhani Gardens is a must-visit spot in Stone Town, Zanzibar, especially in the evening when the lively night food market comes to life. Located along the scenic waterfront, it’s the perfect place to experience local culture, delicious Swahili cuisine, and a vibrant atmosphere.
The highlight here is the fresh seafood grills, where you can try everything from lobster and prawns to octopus and tuna skewers. Don’t miss the famous Zanzibar pizza, a unique street food snack, or the refreshing sugarcane juice.
Beyond the food, the gardens offer stunning sunset views over the Indian Ocean, with local musicians and performers adding to the charm. It’s safe, welcoming, and a great spot to relax after exploring Stone Town’s historic streets.
If you’re in Zanzibar, Forodhani Gardens is the perfect place to taste the island’s flavors and soak in the local vibe! 🌴🌊🍢 #ForodhaniGardens #ZanzibarFood #StoneTown

The highlight here is the fresh seafood grills, where you can try everything from lobster and prawns to octopus and tuna skewers.
Don’t miss the famous Zanzibar pizza, a unique street food snack, or the refreshing sugarcane juice.
Beyond the food, the gardens offer stunning sunset views over the Indian Ocean, with local musicians and performers adding to the charm.
It’s safe, welcoming, and a great spot to relax after exploring Stone Town’s historic streets.
If you’re in Zanzibar, Forodhani Gardens is the perfect place to taste the island’s flavors and soak in the local vibe!

content: I would just like to ask everyone to be extra cautious with what is happening to the Forodhani market. This is an open-air food market right in front of the Old Fort and right by the sea which operates from 18:00 to 23:00. There have been several incidents where sellers tried to charge tourists with crazy amounts of money, so you should ALWAYS ASK FOR THE PRICELIST BEFORE YOU TALK TO THEM FURTHER. Each bench has a pricelist but they hide it under the table so that they can charge you whatever they want. They will try to put a plastic plate on your hands and then put staff on it, and then they will say 'ok let me warm them up for you'" and in no time you have already ordered without you even noticing. Then they bring you back the plate and they ask you to pay an enormous amount of money.

content:
Out of all the experiences in Zanzibar, this one was my favourite.
It was my first time zip-lining, and no better place to do it than in the land of your descendants.
I was with my family, and we ran into the director whilst we were there. They shared what it took to bring this experience to life in Zanzibar and what their visions are going forward. Greatly appreciate them sharing their insights.
The members of the team who took us through the forest were also so friendly and informative. One of my family members was imploring them to make it known that “this is the world’s LONGEST single span zip line in East Africa”.
It was incredibly beautiful to see a part of Zanzibar from above, but walking through it was also curative.
There are several trails, some of which are a little difficult, but the plants and animals will make you overlook this and propel you to challenge yourself.
I would do it all over again.
There were quite a few things under construction, e.g. restaurant, zip line end, etc., when I was there, so hopefully when I return, it’ll be good to see the new additions and enhancements.
Please DO NOT build the viewpoint, I personally don’t think it’s necessary. From where we were standing, it was a sufficient view (less is more in this case).

If you like walking, nature and monkeys, this is a must visit place.

I’ve pretty much spent my whole life standing on all kinds of boards, and Joao picked up on that straight away and adapted the coaching to my level instead of just running through some standard beginner program. Really appreciated that.
Had an absolute blast, learned a ton and got properly hooked. Definitely coming back.
Joao, if you’re reading this: next time I’m showing up as an advanced foiler 😂 Thanks for casually introducing me to yet another hobby I’m gonna spend way too much time on.
TL;DR: 10/10. Super fun, great coaching, would 100% recommend.
Cheers,
Daniel

content:
Very nice location in the middle of the beach and good friendly and laid back school manager and teachers. Joao did a great job and was patient with us. Prices are steep though. Had lots of fun and great experience overall.
One thing I’d like to point out is that the school or rather the instructors should ensure that if you pay for two hours’ tuition, you actually get two hours of active instruction. We actually started lessons late on a regular basis – partly due to preparations, choosing the right kite and walking to the training spot, or simply because everything moved at a slower pace and last time I checked we literally started the lesson with a 15 min delay (which is totally fine, as it’s all ‘pole pole’ and ofc preparations are also part of the learning), but we’d then finish early and were, so to speak, already out of the water before the end of the two hours, meaning you effectively only had 1.5 hours of lessons (sometimes it felt like just one hour). I understand that other people might have a lesson session afterwards, but in future it should be planned a bit more efficiently.

Great school, kind people and high quality equipment.

I arrived in Zanzibar after a difficult period, and thanks to kitesurfing I feel much better now. Part of the credit goes to this place, but above all to the people. Leaving is truly hard: here I found friends, not just instructors.
Thank you from the heart to all of you. For the kite, the support and the atmosphere you created.
Can’t wait to come back.🙏🤘

content:
We had an amazing experience at Kite Centre Zanzibar this month. My two sons (13 and 16) took their very first kite lessons here, and it couldn’t have been better. Their instructor, Joao, was fantastic – clear in his instruction, patient, and great with the kids.
Everything about the school is super well organized: booking was easy, the welcome was warm, payment smooth, and the lessons started right on time. The centre is run by Baris and Stephanie, who are incredibly hospitable and make you feel right at home.
The school is located at Mr Kahawa boutique hotel and restaurant, which has a relaxed surfer vibe and is a great spot for both kiters and non-kiters. The restaurant is excellent – delicious food and friendly service – and it’s set directly on what must be the best beach in Zanzibar. While the kids were on the water, we parents enjoyed chilling, swimming, walking along the beach, and having great meals.
And of course, Paje is the place to be on Zanzibar: lively and buzzing, with all the facilities you need, but still laid-back and enjoyable. Yes, there are plenty of beach vendors (as everywhere on the island), but it’s part of the local charm.
Highly recommended for both learning to kite and simply enjoying the vibe of Paje!

content:
Unbiased, honest review after spending 7 days here: Kite Center Zanzibar is hands down THE BEST KITESURFING CENTER in all of Paje! 😊 WE ABSOLUTELY LOVED SPENDING OUR DAYS HERE!
My friends and I came to Zanzibar on a 7-day holiday to do kitesurfing. We did a lot of research before hand and decided we will be using Kite Center Zanzibar as our preferred choice throughout our stay. Little did we know, this was the best decision we have made throughout this trip! Even after arriving to Zanzibar, on our first day we went to check out multiple schools on the beach (B4, Aquaholics, and several others). However, none were as friendly and accommodating as the team over at Kite Center Zanzibar.
We were first greeted by Stephanie! Who is super friendly, always smiling and easy going - an absolute pleasure to deal with! She explained to us all details about the spot, entry point to the lagoon, location of the reef, areas with seaweed farms (a place you should not go to during low tide), and all other aspects of where to ride in the lagoon. She also gave us a walk around the center and where all facilities were. We later met Baris whom we were also dealing with on daily basis and he was very kind and friendly with all our requests and inquiries. The crew on the ground helping us out (especially Saeed) were super kind and looking out for us all the time!
My friend and I know how to kite so we brought our gears with us. We rented a locker for the entirety of the week and it was brand new and clean. Felt very safe keeping our gear there.
Our 3rd friend is new to kitesurfing so he took the beginner course with their team members and absolutely loved it. They have very clean, well maintained equipment for students (walkie talkie, helmets, vests, etc). My other friend also took a 1-hour advanced lesson with Coach Mohammed to learn transition and he managed to do it from the first trial!! Absolutely brilliant! 😁
I personally rented a 17m kite on the days with low wind and it was in great condition!
Honestly, this was our first time in Zanzibar and it was such an unforgettable experience, mainly because we spent a great deal of time (most of our mornings) at Kite Center Zanzibar with Baris, Stephanie and the rest of the team!! We loved it so much that we wanted to extend a few more days but we had to return home for work :( - Next time inshAllah!

content:
Kite Centre Zanzibar is a kite school/centre in Paje, Zanzibar which uses Duotone/Ion equipment. I rented their equipment during my stay in Paje and was satisfied both by the quality and politeness of the staff. Barish (the manager) and Stefy were really helpful, polite and fun people, sharing the passion of kitesurfing. True kiters, not some impersonal business outsiders, there to make money! Their local spot knowledge was invaluable and their help choosing the right equipment based on the conditions was spot on.
Kite Center Zanzibar uses the most recent Duotone kites, bars and boards and Ion harnesses and wetsuits/lycras. Their rental equipment was in a very good condition and their prices were very reasonable (time starts when first in the water and ends when out of the water - preparation time is not charged).
As a conclusion, I highly recommend Kite Centre Zanzibar in Paje to all that want to learn to kite and even those that want to hang out or rent equipment from people that share a real passion for the sport!

Another really important thing: all the staff at K.C.Z. are helpful and friendly, always ready to raise your kite and lower it, and always ready to give you suggestions for kite size due to the wind forecast!
In short.....the best of what you might want!!!

content:
🏄‍♂️🪁 Three Weeks of Kite Fun:
During my extended stay in June 2024, I rented kite equipment from Kite Centre Zanzibar, and let me tell you—it was three weeks of pure kitesurfing euphoria! 🤩 The gear? All Duotone branded, top-notch quality, and in impeccable condition. 🙌
🤝 Friendly Faces Everywhere:
Baris, Steffi, and the whole staff were like a kitesurfing dream team. Super friendly, fun, and always ready to provide tips on how to nail my next jump! 🏄‍♂️🚀 Thanks for everything!
🌊 Double the Fun:
Paje, oh Paje! This place is a kitesurfer’s paradise. The winds in late June were on point, and you get to kite on not one, but often two totally different waters on the same day 🌊 The flat lagoon is perfect for beginners, while the choppy water (thanks, tides!) adds an extra thrill for advanced riders.
🏝️Stunning lagoon views and great location:
Imagine kiting with a stunning view, the lagoon vista is straight-up magical. Also right next door is Mr. Kahawa, where you can refuel your energy levels after those intense sessions ☕ while enjoying the views - believe you won’t ever get enough of it (and yes I already miss it!) 🌅 And if you’re lucky you might even see some cute monkeys around 🐒
💰 Quality Comes at a Price 💰 Yes, the prices lean toward the higher end, but honestly, it’s worth every of your hard earned Shillings. When you’re soaring through the air, harnessing the wind, you’ll know why. 🚀
So, grab your board, catch the breeze, and let Kitecenter Zanzibar elevate your kitesurfing game! 🌬️🏝️

content: It started with us arriving at the kite centre and finding that no one there had taken our first day of lessons into account. So, someone had to be rounded up immediately so we could start a relatively expensive course (after later asking locals for prices and searching at kite schools in the Netherlands). We had never kited before and received no theoretical explanation whatsoever, nor did anyone warn us about the severe risk of sunburn here (even though the owners are Dutch). It was very annoying, because I still had to go into the water for another two days after that. Now, two months later, those severe sunburns are still visible (and yes, I did apply sunscreen and wore a t-shirt). No one was willing to help at any point. This also became apparent when I was forced to buy a long-sleeved shirt in their shop for €60. Even then, they wouldn't help me properly in the shop, as is customary in a store. Especially a shop like this at a dive school. After almost a week in Paje, we ran into the owners regularly, and while we said 'hi,' they didn't say a word. I see few bad reviews otherwise, so perhaps we just had bad luck with various things. Maybe we had a bad week with setbacks? We didn't speak to anyone anymore and just quietly finished our kite course. That was fine otherwise, and the equipment was good too.

content:
Fantastic kite school, like all the Duotone ones.
The owners are really helpful and always gave us good advice!
Excellent sails, decent boards, harnesses and impact kites that could use some updating, friendly and helpful beach boys.
I rented, while my girlfriend took lessons with Tom.
She made great progress.
Overall, the spot is highly recommended for those just learning, as low tide really helps with board recovery.
You can kite at both high and low tide.
Strangely, we had bad weather at the beginning of January and didn't always get out.
We always used sails:
-13-15 for the lightest ones
-15-19 for the heaviest in the group
In any case, the sea and spot are highly recommended.
They prefer cash payment, as otherwise they charge an additional 3% commission.

content:
I recently spent 14 days kiteboarding at this incredible spot in Paje, Zanzibar, and I have to say it exceeded all my expectations. The beach is stunning with a vast lagoon that offers plenty of space for kiteboarders. I was fortunate to stay at a hotel on the same premises, so accessibility was a breeze.
One of the best things about this spot is how uncrowded it is, offering a serene environment for both beginners and experienced kiteboarders. I rented my gear here, and the equipment was either new or nearly new, with excellent performance and safety features.
The water conditions were generally calm, with little to no chop, and only small waves during high tide. Wind conditions varied, but that actually helped me learn to kite in different settings, under the guidance of their extraordinarily helpful and friendly instructors.
Safety is a high priority here. The team is vigilant and always available to help, ensuring everyone has a good time while prioritizing safety.
Overall, I give this kiteboarding spot a full 5 out of 5. My highlight was gaining the confidence to kite independently under different wind conditions. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this place to family and friends; it’s a kiteboarding paradise!

content: Since my last kitesurfing experience was five years ago, I decided to take a beginner's course at Kite Centre Zanzibar. The positive vibe and friendly, family atmosphere made us feel right at home. While I was out on the water, the rest of the family relaxed on the lounge terrace and in the adjoining café/restaurant. Ahmed was the best kitesurfing instructor anyone could ask for; he selected the perfect equipment and coached me with helpful advice. After two or three hours, I was (back) able to sail independently and confidently across the lagoon, enjoying this tropical paradise with a huge grin! My wife then rented some equipment, which was also incredibly easy. We found the prices reasonable, especially since one of the beach attendants was always on hand to help and everyone kept a watchful eye on you while you were on the water. In short, we all had a fantastic time and would love to come back!

content: I went to Zanzibar for a week to learn kite surfing. I had my eyes already on this school but hadn't pre-booked anything. When I arrived in Paje, I just walked in and was welcomed very warmly. The staff is very friendly, relaxed and flexible. They ran me through my options and I ended up taking 2-hours sessions every day for 5 days. It was my first-time kite surfing and I didn't know what to expect really. My instructor put a lot of emphasis on making me feel comfortable and safe and adjusted the sessions to my learning speed. Once I managed the water start, they installed a walkie talkie on my helmet so that I could stay in touch with my instructor which gave me a lot of reassurance. I had lots of fun in the water and it's a nice feeling if someone guides you while slowly becoming more independent and cheers for you through a mic for each of your small successes. In terms of bookings and payment - you can book your sessions for the next day after your session. They will recommend you the times depending on your level, the tides and the expected weather conditions - so the more flexibility you have the better. Payment can be done via card (5% surcharge like all of Zanzibar apart from Stonetown) and cash. The school is Dutch hence you might want to find out if you can do bank transfer to a Euro account. If you are new to water sport, they also run a small shop where you get the right water wear for your experience.

content:
*I highly recommend this kiteschool!*
We ended up at the kite centre zanzibar after having talked to several other (including cheaper) kiteschools, and I'm happy we did!
During the introductory talk Barış was very honest about the conditions and type of lessons that we would need (since we were not completely beginners). This was in contrast to some other places we've talked to, where it sometimes felt like a rip off..
My instructor Yunus was great! Good in communication, clearly very knowledgeable about kiting but also as a teacher (knows when to push you or stop you) and passionate to make me an indipendent rider.
Planning of lessons was flexible, gear was good. As said, there are schools where you pay less per hour, but in the end we were probably off cheaper due to the high quality of the lessons (and therefore less hours needed) :)
So, if you want proper lessons & gear from knowleable & fun staff, this is the place to be in Paje!

content:
This October our family and a friends’ family booked a 2 weeks holidays in Zanzibar. None of us had ever Kited before, but we went with the intention of learning.
Baris was the guy that welcomed us and helped us make a program for the time there. In the first day he went out and showed us how to control the kite, etc.
After that, his instructors took over and did a great job on the water with us. With a lot of patience and good technic they taught us everything.
Baris was always observing us to make sure we were having fun and learning. The instructor Mo did a great job teaching me everyday in the water and Baris complemented it amazingly: with some simple yet really important tips and some explanations he was the one that made me ride the board for the first time. The guy is not only good in what he does, but also a cool guy. His goal seems to be you fall in love with the sport.
If you have zero experience in kiting and want to learn having fun, go to Zanzibar, go to the Kite Center and see all to Baris. He’ll help you get there!

content:
Me and my husband took a 3-day beginner course at Kitecenter Zanzibar in February 2021. We were so happy with this kite school! Our instructor Baris was a really cool and fun guy but at the same time he was such a professional - he always watched after us, explained everything into detail, kept repeating the steps with us until we got better and was very responsible. This was especially important to me because at first I was quite scared of the kite. Baris made me feel safe and made it fun at the same time :)).
My husband took a short private lesson the last day, Baris gave him instructions via a walkie talkie and I could see that my husband made such a huge progress during this short lesson!
I'm really happy we opted for Kitecenter Zanzibar which is a high quality school. When practicing, we saw some instructors from other cheaper schools which were acting so irresponsibly when teaching tourists. One of them actually crashed its kite into my husband's because they simply don't follow the general safety rules. Please don't try to save money on kitesurfing lessons, it can get dangerous and you also won't learn much.

content:
Matemwe Beach is probably one of the most beautiful beaches on all of Zanzibar, comparable to the northern beaches and the area around Mnemba Island. The turquoise water and white sand are truly stunning.
Unfortunately, there is a significant problem with plastic waste. Large amounts of trash can be found on the beach, and the locals do not seem to care much about it. We tried to clean up some of it ourselves but eventually stopped when we noticed that holes are dug in the sand at night to bury the garbage. Additionally, during high tide, a river further north appears to be used to flush the village’s waste directly into the ocean.
Another downside is the constant presence of sellers. While they are generally friendly, they are extremely persistent and quickly become exhausting.
You should urgently pay attention to low and high tide. Otherwise, it is sometimes not possible — or even dangerous — to enter the water. In addition, you should expect sea urchins.
Zanzibar has incredible natural beauty, but the local population still has a lot to learn when it comes to environmental protection and respectful interaction with tourists.

content:
The ultimate rip-off with guidebooks... You read about a long, beautiful 10km beach, see a few well-framed photos, and the dream seems complete... But what a disappointment when you arrive! Yes, it's 10km long... But there's nothing on the beach, not a single sun lounger or tourist... The reason is simple. It's constantly windy, and most of the time it's low tide... So swimming is completely impossible... A nightmare!
In short, don't make the same mistake I did, and under no circumstances should you stay in a hotel there. There's nothing to do, not a single restaurant, nobody around, and you can't even swim while you're stuck inside your hotel... What's more, the beach isn't maintained at all!
In short, it's not worth the trip, not even for a few hours! Avoid it!

content:
Best spice farm tour in Zanzibar! Ask for Ibrahim to be your tour guide, he is fanatastic! If you do the Tangawizi Bistro cooking class with Shara (highly recommended!) she can request Ibrahim for you.
I did this tour in conjunction with Shara’s Tangawizi Bistro cooking class. Shara (the cook) met me at the market in Stonetown to create the menu and shop for the food and while she set up I did this spice tour. One of the highlights of my trip! All the people here are artisans from the handmade flower baskets to collect your spices and herbs in to the sellers of the soaps and oils and spices straight from the village. Ibrahim is so knowledgeable, funny, excellent English and an overall great tour guide. I loved the end where a guy climbed a coconut tree singing a traditional song and brought down coconuts for us to eat and drink. Bring cash to tip them, they deserve it and it’s all so worth it! Also cash to buy spices, perfumed oils and handmade lotions and other great items. Much of my souvineers came from here and everyone loved the authentic gift I brought back. I did 3 spice farm tours and this one blew me away and it was all because my amazing guide, the talented artesians you meet along the way and Shara’s cooking class where I got to cook with my collected herbs 🌿 💖😊 it’s an amazing experience and one not to miss!

We booked the Stone Town tour and were absolutely thrilled. Our guide spoke excellent German, even though he'd never left the island. Huge respect for that! We had all the time in the world and afterwards even visited a spice farm. I highly recommend booking here and forgetting GetYourGuide.
Two days later.
Mnemba Island.
Again, perfectly organized. Forget the other tour operators. I've never experienced such perfect tours anywhere else. The price is right, the service is superb, including punctual pickup.
I also don't know why people keep saying the dolphins are hunted. While snorkeling, we could see it very clearly. The dolphins stay in the depths and travel in large groups. They surface briefly to breathe and then disappear again. It all happens at a very slow pace, and they are completely calm and uninterested in all the boats. Pure wildlife.

content:
My boyfriend and I went on an excursion today. We were supposed to go snorkeling, have lunch and relax on a sandbar, and visit the mangroves.
We took the boat, but the sea was very rough! In the end, we just went to the sandbar where we stayed for three hours. It was so windy, the sand stung our skin. Like many other tourists, we wanted to head back right after lunch because the situation is very unpleasant. The sea was incredibly rough again, and we spent an hour on the boat with water splashing in our faces, praying we'd get back safe.
This agency seems only interested in money and not in the safety of its tourists. When it came time to pay the bill, the man said he was sorry.
The only positive points were the meal and the captain, who was relatively nice.

All transfers to and from our hotels were very easy and smooth, and all of our drivers arranged by Rafiki tours were very friendly.
Our experience on the Mikumi Safari was unforgettable, we had an amazing Safari with our brilliant and very informative guide, and the flight to Tanzania was very exciting in the small planes.
Prison Island was also brilliant, it was very nice to see how well looked after all of the giant tortoises are. Our guide was very informative and passionate about telling us all about the history of Zanzibar and prison island.
We didn't love our experience on the Mnemba island day trip as much as our other tours, but this does not seem like a common opinion, so we were probably just unlucky on the day having a relatively new and inexperienced guide. Despite this, the coral reef snorkelling was amazing and we thoroughly enjoyed it.
The constant communication with a member of the team throughout our time in Zanzibar was very helpful, and any questions we had were responded to very quickly.
Thank you so much to Rafiki tours, we highly recommend their excursions.

content:
We booked a private trip. The driver was punctual, guides were friendly and helpful and tried to be accommodating. Other than that, it was a bad experience. The snorkeling equipment was terrible and most of it didn’t fit or was poor quality. We felt very unsafe because the snorkeling areas were so crowded with boats, we had to worry about being crushed between boats or run over. There were so many other people, we kept swimming into others and getting kicked. The reef is mostly dead, and the only reason we saw a lot of colorful fish was because the guides were feeding them, which I consider to be really unethical. People were stepping on the reef, partly because the water was too shallow. We told the guide we weren’t interested in trying to find dolphins as we weren’t interested in chasing them.
I think our experience would have been the same with any tour company. If you care at all about the natural environment, I’d advise saving your time and money and not doing any snorkeling trips to this area. I know that local people are just trying to make a living, but it’s so unfortunate that the government of Tanzania doesn’t care enough to regulate tourism so that the reef will be protected for the future.

content:
We booked the trip to Pengume Island and the dolphin swim with Rafiki Tours.
We booked through Instagram and paid via PayPal, which was very convenient and trustworthy!
We were picked up promptly at the agreed time and headed straight to the dolphins, which weren't far away.
There were about 10 boats with tourists there, which made us feel a bit like hunters. We had a private boat to ourselves, which was very nice.
Snorkeling mask, mask, and fins were provided, although I would recommend bringing your own equipment.
Since the dolphins are very fast, swimming with them was rather hectic: the boat comes close, you jump into the sea with your gear, watch the dolphins swim past you for about 30 seconds, and then have to climb back onto the boat (relatively tiring, even for young people). This process is repeated until you say you want to stop.
It's also worth mentioning that no life jackets were provided, which was the case with other tour operators.
After that, we went back to the shore and loaded tables, chairs, and provisions. Then we went to the mangroves near Pengume Island and even saw two monkeys. Next, we went to a snorkeling spot: however, all the coral was dead, and only a few fish were visible. This spot was frequented by several boats, meaning it was operated by other companies.
Afterward, we went to a place where we could see starfish. Then we went to a sandbar with stunningly beautiful blue water, where we were treated to delicious grilled seafood and other treats.
Afterward, we were dropped off by boat at our hotel, as it was low tide. All in all, a fantastic excursion, and booking directly was about €30 cheaper at €80 per person than booking through the hotel reception.
Furthermore, the two captains were very friendly and accommodating. 100% recommended.

content:
I want to warn other travelers about this experience.
We specifically chose this tour because we were told that snorkeling would be the main activity. We also made it clear that we did not want to see dolphins, as we strongly disagree with the way dolphins are chased by tourist boats in Zanzibar.
Despite this, our guide took us straight to the dolphins. What we witnessed was shocking: around 40 boats surrounding and chasing the dolphins. Tourists were instructed to jump into the water between moving boats in an attempt to get close to them. It felt dangerous for both the tourists and the dolphins. The animals were clearly being harassed and stressed. This should not be promoted as a tourist attraction.
After this disappointing experience, we finally went snorkeling. Unfortunately, the snorkeling spot was completely unsuitable. The current was extremely strong, making it difficult and exhausting to swim. There were also huge numbers of jellyfish, and we were stung repeatedly. To make matters worse, we could constantly smell fuel and engine exhaust from the many boat motors around us while snorkeling, which completely ruined the experience and raised concerns about the environmental impact on the marine life. Even worse, our guide disappeared and was nowhere to be seen while we were struggling in the water. It felt genuinely unsafe.
At that point, we were already upset and told the guide that we wanted to return to the hotel immediately. This seemed to cause panic among the guides, as they clearly did not expect tourists to complain or refuse to continue. We had a serious argument before they finally agreed to take us back.
Please be aware of what you are supporting when booking these tours. Chasing dolphins with dozens of boats is not wildlife tourism—it is animal harassment. The noise, fuel fumes, and constant disturbance are harmful to both the animals and the overall experience. If you care about animal welfare, responsible tourism, and safety, I would strongly recommend avoiding this activity.

The “Blue Safari” dolphin tour in Tanzania is sold as a magical chance to swim with dolphins in their natural habitat but the reality is very different.
Dozens of boats chase the same dolphins at the same time. Instead of a peaceful encounter, the animals are surrounded and stressed, constantly trying to escape. Many even appear injured.
This is not respectful wildlife interaction, it’s harassment. Humans with engines versus wild animals trying to survive.
No one should support this. If you truly care about animals, please think twice before booking it.

content:
Mbemba was the first stop on our wonderful stay in Zanzibar, and believe me, the most spectacular along with the Blue Lagoon Safari, which I'll tell you about later.
When we arrived on this wonderful little island, we were immediately captivated by the spectacular white strip of sand that cuts into the ocean for a few hundred meters.
Turquoise water, a coral reef with countless varieties of tropical fish, and, as if by magic, we saw a colony of dolphins happily dancing in the distance, undeterred by the thought of us seeing them.
Perhaps they're accustomed, but they're also docile and less afraid of human presence than other cetaceans.
We immediately set off on the boat to get up close and take some photos. The tour guides also invited us to dive in and swim with them, which initially left me perplexed, but we were reassured; the dolphins here are accustomed, so my children and I jumped in immediately with immense joy.
It was a pure spectacle, magnificent to be so close. and watch their pirouettes underwater.
We stayed in this stretch of water for a good half hour, then the dolphins disappeared.
We returned to the Mbemba sandbar, relaxed and sunbathed on the beach. Afterwards, the program included snorkeling in the coral reef, which is truly extraordinary for its rich coral and fish of every kind and color.
After snorkeling, the excursion concluded with lunch on the island, which was entirely seafood-based. We've never eaten so many lobsters and sea squirts as in Zanzibar, as I believe in many other tropical countries.
Everything was truly top-notch.

content:
I visited Fumba on my last evening in Zanzibar and it's quite a great place for family outing with lots of kid's entertainment. The location is awesome with nice evening breeze Zanzibar has to offer. It is open to public on the weekends but despite the amazing facilities on offer the management has failed terribly in putting in place any simple waste management methods. Vendors of all kinds are allowed to sell their merchandise on site, majority being snacks sellers but the sad fact is with no proper waste management in place all the snack wraps are lazily dropped on the ground by the clueless revellers and swept away by wind into the ocean. Some even throw their waste directly into the ocean. The estimated number of people during my visit was over 500 of which I was made to understand sometimes goes higher.
The management must do something about this, but all in all it's a great family getaway!

content:
I flew to Zanzibar from the US to visit my brother who was in the hospital. He passed away while I was on the way which created a very difficult situation in many ways.
Serenity Funerals was referred by the attending doctor and from the very beginning, all the information I received from them was on point. It was a big help that they knew the right people who were involved in the overall process so there were no surprises.
Not knowing the local language and it being my first time in Zanzibar, this was huge help. In fact, other people continued to offer advice on what I should do and how things worked but in each case, Serenity Funerals was on top of it with the correct information and steps to take. In the end, I was able to experience a very nice service for my brother which I streamed back to friends and relatives at home.
People at home were amazed how much was accomplished in a week...it was all Serenity working with local contacts that knew my brother to make it all come together.
I can recommend Serenity Funerals with full confidence they will come through.

content:
Africa House Garden is a beautiful place with an amazing view and a very relaxing atmosphere. The coffee aroma alone draws you in, and the free WiFi is a great bonus if you want to sit and work or unwind. I ordered a café latte, and it was excellent, very creamy and delicious. The shawarma was okay, not bad, but not particularly memorable.
Unfortunately, the service really took away from the experience. When I first asked for a minute to decide on food, the waiter left the menu and completely forgot about me. I later asked another waiter to call him so I could place my order; he said he would, but he also forgot. After about 40 minutes, I saw the original waiter again and had to remind him myself before my order was finally taken.
The same issue happened when it was time to pay. It was too hot outside, so I moved indoors and asked several waiters sitting near the counter to bring me the bill. All of them forgot and continued chatting. Eventually, when I was about to leave, I asked if it was okay to go without paying, only then did they laugh and finally bring the bill.
The location, view, and coffee are truly lovely, but the service needs serious improvement to match the quality of the setting.
