Navigating the labyrinth of narrow, sun-drenched alleys in Stone Town to suddenly find the towering twin spires of St. Joseph’s Cathedral felt like an unexpected architectural plot twist.

content:
I was wandering around Stone Town and came across St. Joseph's Cathedral—the one with the two towers visible from afar, walking from the market toward the sea.
I didn't go inside, but even from the outside, you can sense the power of the place. Stone walls, slightly darkened by sun and salt, and the scent of the ocean wafting from the street right to the gates.
Standing at the entrance, you can immediately imagine how it was built: the late 19th century, the heat, French missionaries laying the foundation stone, surrounded by sandy streets and the hum of a port city. And now—the same cathedral, the same towers, and seagulls above them, just like then.
I wanted to go inside, but the doors were closed that day. So I stood outside, listening to the hum of the organ and children's voices coming from within.
There's something powerful about it—as if history hasn't ended, but lives on, quietly, within these walls.

content:
St. Joseph's Cathedral, located in Stone Town, Zanzibar, is a significant historical and architectural landmark. Constructed by French missionaries between 1893 and 1898, the cathedral's design was inspired by the Marseille Cathedral in France, evident in its prominent twin spires that dominate Stone Town's skyline.
The cathedral's interior once featured paintings depicting scenes from the Old Testament. However, these artworks were unfortunately destroyed during a restoration in 2014. The building materials, including tiles and stained glass windows, were imported from France, reflecting the European influence on its construction.
Situated in the Baghani area off Kenyatta Road, the cathedral remains an active place of worship for the local Catholic community, hosting several masses each Sunday and occasionally on weekdays. Its twin spires are easily visible from various vantage points in Stone Town and from the ocean, making it a notable feature of the city's landscape.
In the narrow churchyard, there used to be a tall palm tree, which appeared in most pictures of the church; the tree was cut down sometime in the 2000s.
As one of the most important historical buildings in Stone Town, St. Joseph's Cathedral attracts numerous visitors and continues to be a testament to Zanzibar's rich cultural and religious heritage.

St. Joseph’s Cathedral is an essential landmark to visit when in Stonetown. The cathedral’s interior boasts a remarkable design that vividly portrays the ancient history as described in the Holy Book, with a clear representation of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
The location of St. Joseph’s right next to an old mosque is a profound testament to the harmonious coexistence of Christian and Islamic faiths in Zanzibar. This proximity highlights the unique cultural and religious tapestry of Stonetown.
I visited the cathedral on a Sunday, and while the worship times listed at the entrance may not always be accurate, it’s important to note that masses are held in both English and Swahili. Sunday services typically begin at 9 a.m., and weekday services start at 6 a.m., although these times can vary.
Visiting St. Joseph’s Cathedral offers not just a glimpse into the architectural beauty and spiritual heritage of Zanzibar, but also a deeper understanding of the island’s diverse and inclusive community.

content:
Is an important historical building located in the Baghani area of Stone Town, Zanzibar. It was built by French missionaries between 1893 and 1898, and the plans were drawn by the same French architect who designed the cathedral in Marseilles, France. The defining characteristic of the cathedral are its twin spires (similar to those of Marseille’s church) which are prominent elements of the Stone Town’s skyline and can be easily spotted from a distance off the coast. The cathedral interior is painted with murals from the Old Testament. The tiles and stained glass windows were all imported from France. The cathedral is in regular use by Stone Town’s Catholic community. There are several masses held each Sunday and occasionally on weekdays.
Ablution facilities need a little work and it can get a little crowded during peak times but a must see when in Stone Town.

place_name: Taxi and Tours with Juma Zanzibar
content:
An exceptional day with Juma! We chose the dolphin tour followed by a barbecue on a beautiful island (sandbar).
Juma's highlights:
He picks you up from your hotel in his comfortable taxi.
He's incredibly reliable (he drives carefully) and punctual.
His boat has two engines, allowing us to get from one place to another faster and, most importantly, before the other boats.
We swam alone with the dolphins; he stops precisely in the open sea and follows us in the water with the boat—it was extraordinary.
His barbecue was fabulous; we even had lobster!
The boat was private for our family, and there were two of them to take care of us.
Finally, Juma speaks perfect English, is very friendly, and genuinely cares about providing a high-quality experience. I recommend him 100%!

content:
We had an amazing time with Juma and his team! They were incredibly friendly, professional and made sure everything was perfect.
Our day started with a boat trip, and on the way to the sandy island, we were lucky to see dolphins. Once we arrived, we went snorkeling and were amazed by the vibrant marine life - colorful fish, corals, and other sea creatures.
Later, we headed to the Sand Bank, where Juma’s team prepared a delicious seafood lunch featuring tuna, shrimp, calamari, potatoes, lobster, and fresh fruits. It was absolutely mouthwatering! We spent 2-3 hours relaxing, swimming in the crystal-clear water, and enjoying the pristine white sandy beach.
On the way back, they took us to see sea stars, which were spectacular. The variety of colors and sizes was truly fascinating. To end the day, we visited the mangrove trees, adding a perfect touch to an already wonderful experience.
This was one of the best trips we’ve had in Zanzibar. We highly recommend Juma’s tours — his team is knowledgeable, professional and ensures a memorable experience.
Asante sana Juma and all the best for you and your team! 🫶🏻

Amazing experience from start to finish! We left early in the morning directly from the beach in front of our hotel, with a crew that took great care of us.

Highly recommended !

What an experience. We were unfortunate in that the wind was blowing hard on the day that we went so that the seas were quite choppy but our guides knew exactly what to do. They even told us to hang back as they said a squall was coming through, which was very true. Saw lots of other tourists and guides running for covers as pounding rain came in, while we were sitting snuggly in the car.
Once out we were fortunate enough to see a pod of 50 plus dolphins. My kids got to swim with them.
The reef was incredible. So many fish. We would have stayed longer but the as the sea was so choppy we headed back to shore. The guide was from Matemwe and he went through his village and showed us his house.

content:
I'm disappointed. We contacted Mago after reading reviews on Google. The reviews couldn't be better. And that was the case at first. We used his services for a few days, went to Jozani, and a few times to Stone Town – he's responsible, communicative, and everything he said he did (his prices are average). From the very beginning, we talked about a trip to Tanzania, to Arusha for a safari. It was two days and one night.
We agreed on Tarangiri and Ngorogoro National Parks, and the price per person, including roundtrip airfare, was $520. For two, it was $1,040. He personally wrote this amount down on a piece of paper. And the price was discussed daily. He asked for $500 upfront (for airfare). He said to pay the rest to the person who would meet us in Arusha. Before departure, I reiterated that I should pay the remaining $540 to the person who would meet us. Mago confirmed this. By this point, I trusted Mago completely and it never even crossed my mind that this man could cheat.
But! When we arrived in Arusha, the man meeting us started demanding $900 ($400 more!), and he even said the safari was scheduled for Manyara National Park, not Ngorongoro. Naturally, I didn't have $400 on me. With a return ticket in two days, and my wife and I standing in the middle of Arusha, our safari had become a major bummer. We immediately called Mago, and he started accusing me of being deaf, saying he'd said $1,400 for two from the start, and that I'd misunderstood and that I should pay. We'd discussed the price of $520 per person (including airfare) with him several times. How he'd turned $520 per person for two into $1,400, I don't know. But from his words, I understood one thing: I was the fool and it was all my fault.
Later, after reading online, I realized it's common practice in Zanzibar to say less to ensure the client buys (and Mago knew our budget was 1,000, and if he'd initially said 1,400, we simply wouldn't have flown). Overall, the safari turned out completely different from what we expected—with a ton of problems to solve. Lying is not nice, Mago! I'm disappointed. I don't recommend using Mago.

We spontaneously went there by scooter during the off-season. Although we turned up without booking in advance, a super friendly guide with very good English was immediately at our side. He not only explained all the spices and plants to us, but also let us experience, smell and taste them. His extensive knowledge of history was impressive. He gave us an excursion into the history, development and slavery of and on Zanzibar. Of course, there are also fragrances, spices and Arimatuc soaps to buy. But it is not intrusive or obtrusive. You are supporting a good cause and, above all, a kind of cooperative with around 20 women who care and cultivate the plants.
The guided tours can also be conducted in Italian or German, as one or two of the guides speak other languages.
I can highly recommend this tour as we felt well informed, and met with the Tourguide a sympathetic local person who also knows other parts of the island very well....

content:
The Blue Lagoon was touted everywhere as a dream tour: sandbank, fruit, snorkeling, seafood BBQ. GetYourGuide was full of top ratings. Sounds like paradise – unfortunately, it was anything but.
It started with our guide simply "handing us off" to the captain on the beach. Because of the low tide, hundreds of tourists had to walk to the boats – a veritable mass migration. Our captain then spontaneously decided to just leave us standing there, because other guides told us to wait. Spoiler alert: Nobody came back.
After 1.5 hours, we were spotted by chance by another guide and promptly "added" to an Italian group.
Then we were taken in a small rowboat to a completely overcrowded dhow. Understandably, the people there didn't want to let us on. Particularly absurd: A couple had booked a private tour for two – and yet they were still stuck on this overcrowded boat with us. Organization at its finest.
So, another transfer: from the rowboat to a small motorboat that took us to a sandbank. No shade, tons of tourists, a quick bite of fruit (yes, they had some), but the mood had long since soured. We stayed for about 30 minutes. The sandbank was so crowded that we wondered how another boat could even dock there.
Afterwards, we wanted to go to the BBQ. Problem: We had no boat left.
So we waited two hours in the blazing sun (sunscreen is highly recommended; the Zanzibar sun is intense). This left us with a grand total of 10 minutes for snorkeling, since the waiting time was, of course, deducted from the actual activity.
The BBQ took place on an island geared entirely towards mass tourism: markets with cheap trinkets, crowds of people, and a food area that made you fear food poisoning rather than look forward to seafood. Not a trace of lobster, tuna, or calamari – we played it safe and got fries. At least they were hard to spoil.
When the captain later came to collect our snorkeling gear, the moment of relief arrived:
"Oh shit – these are the people I lost."
No joke. After that, there was a frantic search for someone who spoke English, half-hearted apologies, we had to leave the nice group, and were put up somewhere else again because this boat was bigger.
Finally, a quick stop in a bay for a dip – very quick – and then finally back.
Conclusion:
This tour is perfectly organized if the goal is to make tourists wait as long as possible, change boats multiple times, and shatter any illusion of a relaxing excursion. Absolute mass processing, no planning whatsoever, zero romance, zero relaxation.
If you want to experience the real Zanzibar: stay away.
If you like chaotic vacations: have fun.

content:
We found this spice farm on Google Maps because of its great reviews, and it turned out to be exactly what we were hoping for.
We specifically wanted a small, authentic, locally run spice farm — not a big tourist operation or a commercialized attraction. And that’s exactly what we got here.
We contacted him via WhatsApp (the number is listed on Google Maps) and the communication was super quick and friendly. We arranged a time for the next day without any complications. He also asked in advance if we would like to stay for lunch and what we preferred — fish, meat, or vegetarian — and mentioned that the meal was definitely worth it.
The price was only $12 per person including lunch, which is honestly incredible value for the experience you get.
At first glance the spice farm almost looks like a simple garden — a bit wild and very natural — but once you start walking through it, you realize how much is actually growing there. There are so many different trees, plants, fruits, vegetables and spices hidden all around the property.
The tour itself was amazing. He is an incredibly friendly and funny host with lots of jokes and even some German skills, which made it extra fun for us. The whole experience was very interactive: we smelled, tasted and tried to guess many different spices and fruits — probably 10 to 15 different things — and we received small samples of many of them as well.
After the tour we sat down traditionally on the floor and were served lunch. Everything was freshly prepared and incredibly delicious. It felt very authentic and homemade, and we were also served tea with the meal.
At the end we had the chance to buy some spices directly from the farm — and the prices were unbelievably fair. For example, I bought eight large, high-quality vanilla pods for only about 2–3€ in total, plus several other spices. It didn’t feel touristy or overpriced at all — quite the opposite.
This place is the real deal: authentic, welcoming and run with a lot of heart.
Absolutely recommended — 10/10.

content:
Beautiful spot. Locals collect starfish and leave them here. Otherwise, you'd have to be really lucky to find one while walking on the reef.
I recommend either going there with the hotel staff or trying to attract a Maasai, who will approach you anyway as soon as you start walking towards the reef at low tide. Of course, you might initially think the Maasai are trying to sell you something. Nope, they'll tell you all about the reef and are great conversationalists. They'll ask you lots of questions, so don't hesitate to ask them too. You'll learn all sorts of things about the language, culture, and the Maasai themselves.
We went with the hotel staff, and some Maasai joined us. They were very helpful, showing us exactly where to go, because depending on the location, it's like a labyrinth with the sandbanks, seagrass, sea urchins, and sharp coral. The Maasai were a great help to us, even with the hotel staff present. They also helped the elderly, supporting them, offering a hand, and so on. At the starfish spot, they posed with us for selfies and took group photos. We talked and laughed a lot. When we got back, we bought quite a few things in their shops to show our appreciation. Thank you to the Maasai who helped us.

content: OK, let me tell you about this place. We were staying at the Royal Mandarin hotel and I started walking towards the low tide when Masai men reached out to me and told me about this place. I saw that it’s real through the comments but let me tell you more details about it. Those men definitely come near you and help you by being very respectful and polite, but they expect money from you. To be honest, they definitely deserve it because they truly take care of you. They show you different sea creatures as you’re getting closer to the starfish spot. They clear out the sea urchins that they’re on your way and they show you the right path. One thing that it’s misleading is that they try and reach you by walking for 50 minutes towards that spot and then when you say that, you’re in a rush to get back, you can get back in 20 to 30 minutes. But I definitely recommend going there. Just make sure that you have enough time to walk to that spot. Stay there and enjoy and then go back. I would say wake up really early because the sun is unbearable at times start walking right there and they even collect all the starfish and bring them to you. I don’t think it’s ethical to touch the starfish at all, but those men definitely do show you their mouth their eyes so they touch them. They also grab them and put them on you to take a picture. They put them on my head on my shoulders and on my hands. And they do make Christmas trees with all the starfish. The starfish look healthy and some are really large so I hope that they have been used to humans touching them. Nevertheless, it’s a really great spot and a really great idea to do in the morning while you’re staying on that side of the beach. Just make sure that you definitely have money on you because reaching that spot is not possible without the Masai. We left them 10,000 in cash each person.

content: This area can be walked out to from the beaches at the nearby hotels such as Ocean Paradise Resort or Tui Blue at low tide. It is quite a walk and there are many other sea creatures to be aware of as you walk, particularly sea urchins which can be very painful if stepped on. There are Massai men on the beaches that will walk with you, guide you through the best route and show you the sea creatures on the way. They are friendly, respectful and caring towards the sea creatures. I was shown the sea urchins, sea cucumbers and clown fish as well as the starfish. The young Massai man that walked us out even insisted I wear his shoes to avoid injury as I had gone out barefoot, which I would not recommend. Altogether we spent about 2 hours enjoying this experience. Taking tourists out to the reef is a large part of the livelihood of these men and their families and so I made sure I paid him fairly for his time and effort.

content:
This extensive archaeological site preserves the remains of a wealthy maritime settlement dating from the 11th–12th centuries.
Around 40 large coral-ragstone houses have been identified, many built around substantial courtyards. Among the ruins is a large structure identified by archaeologists as the palace of the local Shirazi governor or Sheha.
A small staircase leads down towards the beach. Carved into the coral ragstone, it features ancient holes thought to have held flagpoles, possibly serving as a navigational beacon or signalling point for incoming dhows.

content: A heartfelt project by intelligent people who are passionate about their country's nature, speak excellent English, and treat guests with warmth and care, who visit this secluded spot in a traditional Zanzibar village called Tazari. I'll be honest, we only learned about this place because we came to see the chameleons and the cave, a 10-minute walk from the farm. The young farmer and his family are just getting started with this project, so our visit felt more like a small donation (just $4 per person). But how wonderful it is to give this money to the workers who, with their own hands, create the opportunity to experience the authenticity of the island's beautiful nature. This is especially gratifying compared to the money we spend on pushy and spoiled vendors of tired beach-themed entertainment at hotels where prices are tenfold inflated. We give the butterfly farm 5 stars not for the luxury, but for the warmth of the project.

content:
We found SurpriseTour via Google Maps. Contact was quick and easy via WhatsApp. We were able to find inspiration on the website and let them know which trips we'd like to take. They responded quickly, and everything was easily customized to our wishes. We took three day trips. The first one took us to Jozani Forest, snorkeling at the Blue Lagoon, and we fell in love with the beautiful starfish at Starfish Beach. The second trip took us to Prison Island, Stone Town, and the Spice Farm. The third trip took us to a seaweed farm, Maalum Cave, Mtende Beach, and a village tour. Each one was a beautiful and impressive place that you simply must see during your visit to Zanzibar. ❤️
Fantastically prepared and guided by Abdul and Alibaba! We were picked up right on time, we had the freedom to decide how long we wanted to stay, and Abdul was a great source of information. He also arranged a boat (with a captain), a guide if needed, and delicious fruit and drinks. Alibaba drove us everywhere in their spacious car (with fantastic air conditioning). A challenge, considering the traffic🫣
Above all, Abdul and Alibaba were friendly and cheerful, and it was wonderful to chat with each other, get to know each other better, and learn more about the culture, way of life, etc. We thoroughly enjoyed these days. Abdul and Alibaba, thank you again for organizing and guiding the wonderful activities, and for your company! If we ever visit Zanzibar again, we'll know where to find you! 😉
Asante sana!🫣

content:
We did two tours with Surprise Tour and were completely satisfied. The first half-day tour was to Mnemba Island with Abdul. The pickup was on time, and Abdul told us a lot about the island, and we could ask him anything. The boat trip was lovely. We were lucky enough to see dolphins and were able to swim right above them. The water off the sandbar at Mnemba Island was simply stunning! There were so many fish to see. The snorkeling was fantastic. Afterwards, we had a delicious fruit platter with lots of fresh fruit. Lunch afterwards was also very tasty.
On the second day, we went with Felix (a German-speaking local). First, we went to Jozani Forest, where it was unfortunately raining, but we still saw some monkeys. Then we went to the spice farm. It was really interesting and worth seeing. We had a lot of fun with Felix! And afterwards, we went to Stone Town, where Felix told us a lot about the city and its history. Tip: If you want to buy spices, don't buy them at the spice farm, but at the market in Stone Town – they're cheaper there ;)
We had to reschedule both tours because our tour operator changed the safari tour to other dates. The rescheduling wasn't a problem at all, and communication via WhatsApp was easy. So all in all, Surprise Tour & Safaris is definitely recommended!!!

content:
Before our holiday, I spent considerable time evaluating various excursion providers in Zanzibar. Given that this was a special family vacation—celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary—I was keen to ensure everything went smoothly. However, I was taken aback by the high prices and the lack of transportation to and from our hotel for most of the excursions. Determined to find a better option, I turned to Google and zoomed in on our village near Paradise Beach Hotel. That's how I discovered Abdul from Surprise Tour and Safari’s.
Abdul provided excellent advice on which combination of tours would best suit our preferences, crafting a wonderful itinerary of five excursions during our 11-day stay in Zanzibar. Abdul is an incredibly friendly young man who shares a wealth of information and genuinely strives to immerse you in the culture and lifestyle of Zanzibar. With his local contacts, Abdul ensures that the tours steer clear of overly touristy spots, allowing for a more authentic experience.
Our transportation was in luxurious taxi buses with friendly drivers, and Abdul carefully planned our excursions according to the tides for the best possible experience. Over five days, our family enjoyed amazing excursions with Abdul as our private guide, providing us with the most authentic experiences we could have hoped for. For us, Abdul was a true stroke of luck.
We also appreciated the flexibility of paying after each excursion.
Our excursions included:
1. Mnemba Sandbank
2. Prison Island, Stone Town, and Spice Farm
3. Jozani Forest
4. Safari Blue
5. Natural Aquarium and dhow boat construction in Nungwi
We wholeheartedly recommend Surprise Tour and Safari’s for an unforgettable and genuine Zanzibar experience and the benefit for local people.

content:
WARNING: extortionist boat ride!
i booked a private catamaran for my friends and family to celebrate my birthday november 2023. i paid US$2000 which converts to over $5 million TZ shilling for an 8hr ride!! for that price i expected a certain level of service.
The Good:
1. the boat was in good condition
2. the chef prepared an amazing lunch that was satisfying and enjoyed by all 24 passengers.
The BAD (and these's much):
1. via email the plan was to be picked up at our hotel's dock. due to the extreme tides in zanzibar this was not a true option. i was dishonest of azam to say it was possible when it wasn't. had i known in advanced, i could have made appropriate transportation plans.
2. poor communication once in zanzibar - i was not given the correct whatsapp number for the captain and VICTORIA the company liaison did not adequately help with facilitating day of communication.
3. we were forced to go to the beach that azam operates from meaning unexpected cost of transportation resulting in a 2hr delay to the start of our ride. upon arrival, NO ONE was there to greet all 24 of us ranging from age 73 to 3! after getting help from a kind employee, we were escorted to small boats that brought us to the catamaran. POOR customer service.
4. we sailed near but not up to mnemba island. i chose NOT to pay extra for snorkling in that area; however half way through our sail, we were detained by what i describe as pirates and neither our captain, nor VICTORIA (via phone) came to our defense but rather appeared to be in cahoots with the pirates to extort money from us. initially the ask was for US$5 per person for our time near mnemba island, however since we never stopped by the island, the asked dropped to US$3. still refusing to pay, the captain spoke with victoria and the pirates and the final settled price was a total of US$50. this back and forth took almost 1HR of the boat ride!! the pirate boat was called 'TOM CAT.'"

content:
For all visiting yachts I would NOT recommend using this Marina.
Rubbish is left rotting on the Dock for many days.
The staff are unhelpful.
Ash from a burning Rubbish Tip lands on your boat every day.
The water is also only working half the time and has terrible pressure. Not ideal if you want to clean your boat.
Also in our case without agreeing a price or understanding the job they completely ruined our new antifoul by scrubbing off completely our soft antifoul, costing us a hugely expensive haul out to Redo it. They apologised but said tough luck mistakes happen.
It is also very far from town and there is no fuel at Marina.
Save yourself the trouble and anchor off.

content:
Mangapwani Slave Chamber Tour
Slave Chambers: Built around 1880 from the cave and connected to the seaside 2kms away, the area is surrounded by varieties of indigenous trees such as Breadfruit, Ramboutants and scent shrubs.
It was an important transit point for the captured slaves to be sold to the outside world at the time of the abolishment of slavery in 1873. Between 1880-1905, the chamber was being used as a place of concealment of the human cargo pending their disposal.
A utilized as the hideout by the Arabs for their human cargo ready for shipment. The four hour guided tour begins and ends at your hotel. Mangapwani (“Arab Shore”) lies in a district where many Arabs used to live.
In the village there is a Police Station, also a large government “Bungalow” which was built by the Arabs who originally owned Prison Island. Newly opened Serena Restaurant is nearby the Slave Caves. Swimming, Sun bathing may be done widely.

content:
We had the most amazing day on the Tamasha Dhow boat trip! From the moment we stepped on board, Natia, her husband, and the entire crew made us feel incredibly welcome. Their genuine hospitality, kindness, and enthusiasm made the experience truly unforgettable.
We were traveling with our own group of eight people (4 kids). Although the boat could have accommodated more guests, we were given the option to keep it private and not have strangers join us.
The trip itself was fantastic. We were lucky enough to see dolphins, and we really appreciated that the crew chooses not to chase or disturb them. Because of this respectful approach, you’re not surrounded by 20+ other boats competing for the same dolphins, which made the experience feel peaceful, authentic, and much more enjoyable.
We also stopped at a beautiful reef where we enjoyed some great snorkeling. On top of that, we were treated to a delicious homemade lunch and fresh tropical fruit later in the day – such a lovely touch!
Everything was perfectly organized, relaxed, and filled with smiles. If you’re looking for an authentic, friendly, and memorable boat trip in Zanzibar, we can wholeheartedly recommend Tamasha Dhow. Thank you for giving us such a wonderful day!

content:
My husband and I visited Stone Town with the hope of finding some meaningful artwork to take home, and we were lucky enough to stumble upon this beautiful boutique gallery tucked away in a quiet alley. The space was small but filled with truly unique and captivating paintings. We explored other parts of Stone Town afterward, but we kept thinking about this gallery and ended up coming back because nothing else compared to it.
We were a bit rushed that day, so the next morning we contacted Othman to ask if it was possible to see more artworks at our hotel, as our friends were also interested and it was too far to return to Stone Town. To our surprise, Othman went above and beyond and arranged a mini pop-up art exhibition right in our hotel car park the very same day.
The collection he brought was absolutely amazing. In the end, we and our friends purchased six paintings in total, and we couldn’t be happier to bring home such special memories of Zanzibar. Abdul, the driver, was incredibly friendly and even helped remove the paintings from the canvases to make traveling easier.
Othman is extremely knowledgeable and passionate, and he took the time to explain the background and stories behind the artworks, which made the experience even more meaningful. This was truly one of the highlights of our trip, and I highly recommend this gallery to anyone visiting Stone Town and looking for something authentic and unforgettable.

content:
Unfortunately, this tour was a huge disappointment. We chose the Nakupenda, Prison Island & Stone Town tour.
The organization was disastrous: Upon pickup, we were quickly charged, shoved onto some random bus, and then disappeared. We had no idea what was going on. There was no plan for who to contact or anything else. Only after asking around did we find out it was the right bus. After a few minutes, the bus stopped at a gas station without informing the passengers. In the end, everyone had to wait 25 minutes simply because two passengers were booked on a different tour.
The bus driver drove like a maniac, completely disregarding safety. Several times we were genuinely afraid of an accident.
Once we arrived at Prison Island, we continued our journey in extremely slow boats. The boats were truly dilapidated and in terrible condition. It was as if their motto was "as long as they don't sink." Seasickness sufferers were already at their wits' end here, as the boats crawled across the sea at a snail's pace, causing extreme rocking. The island itself is run-down, overcrowded, and not very appealing.
Afterwards, we went to the Nakupenda sandbank. Instead of a dream island with clear water, it was overcrowded, with greenish-murky water, and vendors constantly pestered the guests, even while eating. Leftovers from lunch were even lying around on the beach (e.g., shrimp heads). Shady spots consisted of makeshift blankets.
The food: Perhaps okay for seafood lovers (lobster, etc.), but not for us. As an alternative, there was chicken – unfortunately inedible: My girlfriend got a small piece with meat, I only got bones with skin and cartilage. Rice and fries were fine, but the fruit was very tasty. We weren't full.
The return trip was also chaotic: A couple who had already kept everyone waiting were late again. The boat left without them, had to turn around, and the man completely lost it – aggressive, insulting, almost violent towards the guide. Very unpleasant for all the other passengers.
The Stone Town tour essentially consisted of rushing through the streets and spending a lot of time in souvenir shops.
On the plus side: The guides (especially Rasheed and Mudi) were very friendly, and there were plenty of drinks and fruit.
In conclusion: A pure mass-market experience with no quality. We were very disappointed, were even afraid at times on the bus, and would recommend the Mnemba Island tour instead – it's beautiful and stress-free.

Ali frequently appears at the supermarket in front of the Malika Hotel, so be careful!

content:
Kendwa Beach on Zanzibar's northwestern coast is a haven for sun-seekers and water enthusiasts. Here's a quick glimpse:
Paradise Found: Imagine soft, white sand beneath your toes, turquoise waters lapping at the shore, and swaying palm trees providing shade. That's the idyllic picture Kendwa Beach paints.
Activities Galore: This beach caters to active spirits. Dive into the crystal-clear waters for snorkeling or scuba diving adventures exploring vibrant coral reefs. For those who prefer staying above water, options like kayaking, stand-up paddleboarding, and kiteboarding due to favorable wind conditions are all on the table.
Relaxation at its Finest: If unwinding is your priority, Kendwa Beach delivers. Stretch out on a sun lounger, listen to the calming rhythm of the waves, and soak up the African sunshine.
Lively Atmosphere: Unlike its neighbor Nungwi, Kendwa boasts a more vibrant scene. Beachside restaurants and bars offer delicious local and international cuisine alongside refreshing drinks. In the evenings, some spots transform with live music and dancing, making Kendwa a great choice for those who enjoy a bit of nightlife after a day of relaxation.
Perfect for All: Whether you crave adventure, relaxation, or a touch of both, Kendwa Beach offers something for everyone. Soak up the beauty, enjoy the activities, and experience the lively spirit of this captivating beach paradise.

content:
One of the most valuable parts of this experience was gaining a deeper understanding of the history of Zanzibar and the slave trade from a perspective that is often missing from Western narratives. The tour provided important context about the complex roles of local kingdoms, Arab traders, European powers, and global demand, helping us better understand the difference between slavery as it existed in various forms throughout Africa and the transatlantic slave trade that reshaped entire societies.
As a family, we appreciated the opportunity to learn, ask questions, and engage with history in a thoughtful and balanced way. The experience challenged assumptions, added nuance, and gave us a greater appreciation for Zanzibar's important place in world history. A meaningful visit for anyone seeking a deeper understanding of the island and its past.

content: Well, to begin with, we did the 1-hour hike. A tourist trap. I don't recommend it. Especially since they tried to trick us as soon as we arrived by saying the tip was mandatory. The tour price is very high for what they offer.

content: Kuza Cave is such an amazing place and a must see, especially if visiting Zanzibar with kids. My son and I spent a whole day and evening there starting with a swim in the ceremonial cave waters which were gloriously clear, a great temperature to swim in & surrounded by an amazing cave. Backdropping the cave swimming is the sounds of Swahili drumming put on by the very talented group at the attached cultural center. We were welcomed into the drumming circle as we exited the cave and immediately provided drums so we could take part. After a quick change of cloths we took a Swahili cooking class which offered us a deliciuos lunch. While I rested my son spent the afternoon engrossed in various art projects centered around both African and global art, history and culture. As afternoon rolled into evening we were invited back to dining room delicious Swahili starters and drinks. We soon moved to an outdoor seating area where we spent the evening immersed in very well thought out, prepared and presented music & theatre performance put on by Swahili locals which provided a deep history of Africa and the origins of human existance. A spectacularly education and relaxing day!

content: A really nice place to visit. The entrance fee is 20.000 shilling (in cash) and the money goes to the community around the cave. We visited before the rain season started so the water level was quite low, but in rain season the water level rises incredibly high (you can see the green algae on some photos taken at the top of the cave), so it would be a completely different experience to come and swim in the rain season. The water is cold when you step in (since the temperature is so high in general), but give it a few seconds and it becomes this really cool and relaxing experience. I’m really glad we went, I’m just glad I remembered to bring cash since they don’t take credit cards (as far as I could see). The water changes from quite shallow to deep in a heart beat (I’m 177 cm and couldn’t stand on half the area), so just know how to swim (or float) or stay close to the edge of the water. Oh, also, this is a natural cave so the stones in the water are sharp, this is not a pool, just so you remember to swim and place your feet carefully 😊 They also sell drinks at the community center before you enter the cave. And there is an old style swahili house you can enter to see how they used to build them (using no metal, just wood, earth, stones, rope and palm leaves)

content:
We visited in January 2021. It's easy to find (the road is right across from the Tina House apartments). Entrance is $10 per person. It's a unique place, and the memories are unforgettable. The water is clear and cool, perfect for this heat! You probably don't need to make a special trip there, but if you live nearby, it's a great experience. We stayed there for one night; we stopped there on the way, and then went to another beach.
The incredible architectural forms created by nature itself are breathtaking. The Kuza Caves are a remarkable natural formation, ascribed mystical properties by the local population.
A freshwater pond, hidden from sunlight by a rock massif on an island amidst salty ocean waves, its very existence evokes thoughts about the origins of natural wonders.
The indigenous islanders have long considered the Kuza Caves sacred. For centuries, religious processions have come here to perform rituals and offer prayers. Ancient legends surround the stone labyrinths, which remain completely unexplored. In the deepening darkness, hidden passages and corridors can be discerned. To this day, several days a year are set aside for traditional ceremonies, when the cave is closed to prying eyes.

For those who enjoy diving, snorkeling, and diving, here's a tip: bring a mask, snorkel, and underwater light. It's fascinating to dive in and sit for a few seconds, feeling like you're in a water cave, a rocky hole completely underwater, with a stone ceiling above your head. It's an adrenaline rush. It's safe if you have good vision, breathing, and orientation. I personally wasn't very interested in just splashing around with the crowd of tourists, jostling in narrow spaces.

It's a bit difficult to get there on foot, but a taxi wouldn't be much of a pleasure and likely wouldn't appreciate the place. There's a shop selling water and beer. The locals put on a short show featuring traditional musical instruments and acrobatics. They charge for it, but it's not pushy, so you don't have to pay.

content: It seems my experience was very different to others. I can only guess with the number of good reviews, perhaps we picked an off day to visit. The cave was one of the first on my list to try and I was disappointed and a little uncomfortable. On arrival I was surprised to feel unwelcome by the staff. This was not the welcome I have come to know of Zanzibar. We paid $20 using a $50 and were told we could get our change on the way out. This seemed a little strange and judging by the less than welcoming feel we encountered, we asked if we might be able to have our money before going in to cave. The young man spoke with a lady who was watching while she cooked and returned to say no, we would get our money later. Perhaps this was all we needed to have a less than pleasant experience in the cave. We were told the water and caves were old and when we asked about the colour, was it the minerals in the caves, the answer was no it was just nature. I'm sorry to leave this review as I wish the organisers well in their contribution to the community from the money from this but it all felt like a lot of money for a 2 minute dip then leave?

content:
A Swahili Cooking Experience Like No Other!
Sharing the Swahili cooking experience at ZanCulinary with my friends visiting from the U.S. was truly special.
From the eco-friendly setting to gathering fresh ingredients straight from the trees — including bananas and sweet jackfruit that Is-Haka climbed up to get for us — every moment felt authentic and joyful.
Making homemade chapati from scratch was such a highlight! And the live violin player blending the latest hits with traditional Zanzibari taarab music created the most beautiful atmosphere.
Chef Lulu was patient, warm, and so much fun, and Omari, the owner — words truly can’t express how grateful I am to have met him. We enjoyed every second.
If you’re looking for an intimate, authentic Zanzibari Swahili cooking experience, ZanCulinary is a must!

content:
Completely lost. We paid €90 for 3 people, and it was supposed to include:
- Boat: It's supposed to be for 10-12 people, but there were about 22 of us.
- Visit to a sandbar with a fruit lunch: We were there for 30 minutes, and the area was packed.
- Snorkeling: I don't think it was the worst snorkeling I've ever done. There were no fish, the coral was dead, and the area was full of some kind of jellyfish that, luckily, didn't sting.
- Visit to the island with the oldest baobab tree: You can see it in 5 minutes, and then they rush you to lunch without letting you explore the island.
- Seafood lunch: They pile you up on rice and fries, then serve you a mini salad, half a mini lobster (it must have been a European lobster, judging by the size), a tiny piece of tuna, 3 prawns, and 4 small pieces of octopus. Nothing like the picture they advertise.
- Visit to the Blue Lagoon with mangroves: The place is beautiful, but you only get access and they give you 15 minutes to swim, without allowing you to walk or boat around the rest of the lagoon.
- 5 beers: After we had already paid, they told us they weren't included and that some of the salespeople always do that to attract customers without actually including them. On top of all this, there were many hours in the sun, little shade, and a completely wasted amount of time.
I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT!

content:
We just finished the Blue Safari excursion, and it was undoubtedly one of the biggest disappointments of the trip.
There were about 30 of us on a traditional boat, all crammed together with very little space to sit. During the first part of the excursion, there was no shade, which made the journey especially uncomfortable. After lunch, they did provide shade for everyone, but some of us had already gotten sunburned.
One of the main attractions, the Blue Lagoon, wasn't visited because, they said, the tide wasn't right. From there, we were supposed to see the mango trees, but we couldn't see them for the same reason. As an alternative, they told us we could swim there since the boat couldn't get close, which isn't a realistic or safe option for everyone, and in practice, we didn't see anything.
Instead, they took us to a supposedly deserted sand island that was completely overcrowded, full of tourists and vendors, with no charm whatsoever and a tourist market atmosphere. A pristine island? Not at all.
The fruit picnic was clearly insufficient and poorly distributed for so many people. Only the quickest ate; some didn't even get a taste of certain fruits. The organization was nonexistent.
The snorkeling is a deception. There's no sign of the coral, colorful fish, and crystal-clear waters shown in the advertisements. It's done among boats, in murky water, surrounded by people, and you always see the same small fish. The seabed is gray, with nothing remarkable about it.
The food doesn't justify the price either. Nothing like a "great seafood feast": rice, potatoes, vegetables, and a few shrimp, octopus, and half a lobster cooked over a fire—a bit dry—with no real option for seconds except for the rice. It was adequate as a basic meal, but far from what was promised.
Finally, the "cultural" part is limited to seeing a baobab tree without any explanation, followed by free time in a shopping area clearly designed to get you to spend money. Nothing more.
Pay €150 for two people for this excursion? Never. This is a completely disproportionate price for a poorly organized, oversold tour focused solely on squeezing money out of tourists.
WE ARE TOURISTS, NOT FOOLS.

We booked the Safari Blue through our hotel for €130 (2 people). It’s advertised as a day of snorkeling in a beautiful sandbank, but the reality was very disappointing.
• Long, wasted travel time: 3 hours to get there and 2+ hours back in a poorly maintained, overcrowded boat with a weak outboard engine. Safety felt questionable.
• Snorkeling is minimal: only about 20 minutes, in an overcrowded area with little to see. Not the highlight they promise.
• Poor equipment: not enough for everyone, and in bad condition.
• Low-quality food: plain white rice, fries, a small piece of tuna and overcooked octopus.
• Overall, a wasted day for what should have been the main activity.
Would not recommend this experience.

content: We booked the Safari Blue excursion through our hotel, and being honest it was the worst experience we’ve had during our time in Zanzibar. The starting location was very difficult to reach, and although you can expect this in Zanzibar, we didn’t know that the whole day would be spent in transport rather than the experience. However, this was certainly not the worst part: 1. We sailed in a poorly kept boat, with more people that it was capable to transport. 2. They took us to an island crowded with people and kept us there for an hour, when apparently the activity was “Safari Blue” = snorkel; 3. The snorkel lasted for no more than 20 mins after which they took us to another island to have “lunch”. (Do not recommend) 4. Again the way back home was extremely long, this time sailing - which should be cool - but it’s not when you are with other 25 people in a packed wooden boat. Although the staff managed to fall asleep… Overall, I would certainly not recommend this experience or the agency it self. It is 100% a tourist trap and wouldn’t waste neither my day nor 130$ for such a poor experience.

Jumping out of a plane over Zanzibar was one of the most intense, beautiful, and unforgettable experiences I’ve ever had. From the moment we took off to the freefall over that unreal turquoise coastline, it was pure adrenaline, freedom, and awe all at once.
A huge thank you to Miguel for making this such an incredible experience, and to the whole team at Skydive Zanzibar for the professionalism, energy, and confidence you gave me from start to finish.
Definitely one for the memories. Zanzibar from the sky is something else.

content:
Skydive Zanzibar was an absolutely unforgettable experience. The whole team was extremely professional, friendly, and made me feel safe from the moment I arrived. The instructors explained everything clearly and kept the atmosphere relaxed, even though it was my first time skydiving.
The flight up to 10,000 ft was beautiful on its own, but the jump… incredible. The views over Zanzibar — turquoise water, white beaches, and the coastline — were truly breathtaking. It’s the kind of moment you never forget.
The landing was soft, the gear felt secure, and the entire process was well-organized. I also got high-quality photos and video shortly after the jump, which was a great bonus.
Overall, Skydive Zanzibar is one of the best adventure activities you can do on the island. Safe, professional, and 100% worth it. Highly recommended for anyone looking for adrenaline and a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

It was my very first time skydiving, and Skydive Zanzibar made it an unforgettable experience. From start to finish, everything felt extremely professional and well-organised, which instantly put me at ease. The team’s attention to detail and calm guidance ensured that the jump was not only safe but also incredibly enjoyable. I especially want to thank my instructor, Miguel, for making the tandem skydive such a fantastic experience—his encouragement and expertise truly made all the difference.
I would highly recommend Skydive Zanzibar to anyone considering the adventure, and one tip I’d give is to definitely get the media package. The short video captured during the skydive will serve as a memory for a lifetime.

I was very nervous going into it but the entire team put me at ease from the moment i walked through the door. Both skydiving instructors are very well educated and know how to do their job to the best of their ability and will explain anything and everything to you if that’s what you prefer. Additionally, the media package is amazing, full of pictures and an entire video of the whole experience from start to finish as well as a short video for social media.
I would recommend Skydive Zanzibar 100 times over. Truly a once in a lifetime opportunity in the most beautiful place.

Huge thanks to Gary for handling everything so professionally—it made the experience stress-free and fun!
Jumping from 10,000 ft, the freefall was the biggest rush of my life! Seeing the crystal-clear ocean below as I soared through the sky was surreal. And landing right on Kendwa Beach at Kendwa Rocks Hotel? Just epic. Big shout for my instructor, Miguel. He was too good
The videos were next level! The 2-minute jump video and the Instagram were perfectly put together. If you’re in Zanzibar, do yourself a favor and book this experience. 100% worth it!

content:
I had an absolutely amazing experience with Skydive Zanzibar! From the moment I arrived, the team provided clear instructions, made me feel safe and comfortable, and - most of all - super excited for the jump.
The view? Absolutely breathtaking! Soaring over the turquoise waters of Zanzibar was nothing short of magical. It’s a sight you have to experience to believe!
A huge shoutout to all three Mike’s, Jason, and Gary—an incredibly professional, high-functioning team that knows how to make skydiving not just thrilling, but also insanely fun. Their energy and expertise truly bring out the joy of the experience.
I 10/10 recommend this to everyone! Whether you’re a first-timer (like I was) or a seasoned skydiver, this is an adventure you must add to your bucket list. If I could, I’d do it all over again right now! ✈️🪂

content:
Negligent, Unsafe, and Completely Inhumane – Only Consider for a Single Tandem Jump
I initially signed up for this company’s skydiving certification course, but it turned out to be one of the worst decisions of my life. While they might be acceptable for a one-time tandem skydive, their training courses are shockingly unsafe and their practices outright negligent.
I was rushed into a solo skydive despite clearly not being ready for it. Their lack of proper training and assessment resulted in a devastating accident that left me hospitalized for 8 days and 7 nights. The physical and emotional toll was immense, but what made it worse was their complete lack of support afterward.
Neither the CEO nor anyone from the team contacted me during or after my hospital stay. I was left alone on the island to cope with the aftermath of their negligence, without a single call, visit, or offer of assistance. Their inhumane and unsupportive behavior made an already traumatic situation even worse.
If you’re just looking for a one-time tandem skydive, they might be okay—but do not trust them for any training or certification. This company cares nothing for your safety or well-being. There are far more reputable and responsible options out there. Avoid them at all costs.

content:
The wait was far too long, which ruined the experience. We had an appointment at 11:30 AM and arrived 15 minutes early as requested. We left the hotel for the airfield at 12:45 PM, an hour and a half after our arrival. It was clear the instructors were completely jaded and that only business mattered. The freefall itself was flawless, but as soon as the parachute opened, it was a mad dash down, not even time to admire the scenery, and it was even more complicated being upside down. Sorry, but I've had better experiences elsewhere.
3 stars for communication with the staff and the scenery, -2 stars for the wait and the descent after the parachute opening.

content:
Even though skydiving was always on my bucket list, taking the plunge was a spontaneous decision. The team is really very professional, just like Denis, who jumped with me. So everything went quickly and smoothly. The view from the plane was amazing and to jump and fall was an incredible feeling!
The landing was soft and all I thought was that it was over too quickly. I recommend everyone to try skydiving, especially in Zanzibar. You don't get to experience something like this everyday with this view on top!
The video, which was recorded by Denis as well, is also dope and helps me relive the dream over and over again. Thanks to the Skydive Zanzibar team, especially Denis - again at any time!

content: I had been putting off skydiving for way to long but I’m so happy I picked Skydive Zanzibar for my first jump. The pre-jump process was very smooth and I felt incredibly safe the whole time. You could tell the staff took all the precautions and paid attention to the details of safety. The instructors (I was with Dennis and he’s a rockstar) took charge from there and were very encouraging and brought a great energy. The plane was very well maintained and flight up had spectacular views. The jump itself was such a rush. Free falling over the crystal clear blue waters was so thrilling and so peaceful at the same time. After the chute opened, Dennis gave me the controls until we were ready to spot the landing. I would recommend this again and again and hope to do another jump with them in the future. I can’t wait to see the video footage and am glad I purchased it because they took a ton of footage and it’s going to be worth every penny. Asante Sana 🤟

The sensation of freefall during the first 30-40 seconds is truly magnificent as you fly through the clouds. Once the parachute is deployed, a breathtaking view of part of the island unfolds before you.
The feeling of flying is simply splendid: letting yourself be carried by the wind while admiring the magnificent landscapes blending Zanzibari villages and idyllic beaches. And to top it all off, a smooth landing on Kendwa Rocks beach. Thank you to Artem for this jump and thank you to the entire SKY DIVE Zanzibar team for their professionalism. Top-notch, I highly recommend it! 👌🏻 Don't be afraid, just go for it! 🤙🏻

content: Knowing what Health and Safety is like in Africa I made sure I done my research. These guys have every major skydiving qualification in the world and are very experienced. My friend is an engineer for the rich and famous’s aircraft so I know a bit about planes although there plane is small more importantly it is mechanically sound and safe and well maintained. The experience was Amazing my friends joked saying how long were you in the air for 1 minute. But we skydived for about 2 minutes and then maybe a 15-20 minute parachute with a guided tour of Zanzibar and all it’s Islands. I could see where I was staying in Stone Town around 30 miles away. The views were Amazing. I am actually scared of heights but the view is so beautiful you forget about that instantly. I jumped with Gary who was very friendly and enthusiastic and knowledgeable on the island and sights we saw. Despite me being scared of heights I felt confident with Gary. He is a great Camera man as well they sent me tonnes of professionally edited photos and videos that would put a James Bond film to shame. Thanks for a great experience!

content: The Old Portuguese Arch in Stone Town, Zanzibar, stands as a subtle yet significant relic of the island’s brief Portuguese era in the 16th and 17th centuries. Located near Victoria Garden, between Vuga Road and Malindi Road, this ancient stone arch is one of the few remaining structures from Portuguese rule, offering a glimpse into a period that left minimal architectural impact on Zanzibar. The arch’s weathered facade and enduring presence provide a tangible connection to the past, inviting visitors to reflect on the layers of history that have shaped Stone Town’s unique cultural tapestry.

content: In the 15th century, in the deep jungles of Zanzibar, the Portuguese discovered an entrance to a subterranean labyrinth connecting to the ocean and began building a village with stone houses nearby. Parts of these buildings have survived since then. Higher up on the hill is the ancient settlement of Fukuchani, home to 2,000 local residents, who primarily engage in agriculture and fishing. The surrounding jungle is filled with 200-year-old baobabs, giant mango trees, banana palms, and other wondrous plants that provide food for the locals. The cave has been modernized with a sturdy staircase, albeit a rather steep one. We arrived at low tide in the Indian Ocean, so only after reaching the very last step were we able to touch the clear seawater. According to the guide, the depth at low tide was 3 meters. But at high tide, the depth of the Okoye water is about 7 meters. At the current time, Meyer and the ruins are used to teach history and geography to schoolchildren. From Nungwi, the site can be reached by tuk-tuk in 20 minutes, for a roundtrip fee of about $15.
